The group's vocalist usually portrays the band's mascot character, a Satanic priest known as Papa Emeritus.<ref name="sfwinterview"/> There have been four different characters taking the name Papa Emeritus. They first welcomed the second Papa Emeritus on 12 December 2012, in Linköping. On 3 June 2015, the second Papa Emeritus welcomed his younger brother as the new Papa Emeritus in Linköping after being "fired" due to not performing his duty in overthrowing governments and churches. Papa Emeritus II and Papa Emeritus III were stated to only have a 3-month difference in age. On 30 September 2017 during a show in [[Gothenburg]], Papa Emeritus III was dragged off stage by two men, who then escorted a new character, Papa Emeritus 0, to the stage to introduce the band's next chapter. Papa Emeritus 0 is portrayed as being significantly older than the previous Papas, making use of a walker and oxygen tank whilst walking on stage. On 19 January 2018, the band shared a video that features a character, implied to be Papa Emeritus IV, listening to ''Ceremony and Devotion'' on [[8-track tape]] while critiquing Papa Emeritus III's vocal abilities. The character's face is hidden offscreen, but he is shown to wear red vestments similar to a [[Cardinal (Catholic Church)|cardinal priest]]. He was later revealed to be Cardinal Copia.<ref name="VH1 classic"/><ref name="Papaganda">{{cite magazine|url=http://noisey.vice.com/noisey-specials/ghost-bc-ep-1|title=Swedish Heavy Metal Band Ghost "Gets Very Euro-Trashy" on the Tour Bus|magazine=[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]]|date=11 September 2013|access-date=29 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131101234404/http://noisey.vice.com/noisey-specials/ghost-bc-ep-1|archive-date=1 November 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> At the final show of [[A Pale Tour Named Death|the tour in support of ''Prequelle'']], Papa Nihil had collapsed and "died", and Cardinal Copia became Papa Emeritus IV. Papa Nihil was later resurrected during the European leg of the [[Imperatour]].<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Merlin|last=Alderslade|url=https://www.loudersound.com/features/satanic-sermons-and-sax-solos-inside-ghosts-first-uk-show-in-two-and-a-half-years|title=Satanic sermons and sax solos: inside Ghost's first post-Impera headline show   |magazine=[[Metal Hammer]]|date=11 April 2022|access-date=11 April 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220411100851/https://www.loudersound.com/features/satanic-sermons-and-sax-solos-inside-ghosts-first-uk-show-in-two-and-a-half-years|archive-date=11 April 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> In March 2025, the band announced in social media that Papa V Perpetua was to be their next frontman.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Gregory|last=Adams|url=https://www.revolvermag.com/news/ghost-set-to-reveal-satanized-new-frontman-papa-v-perpetua/|title=Ghost set to reveal "Satanized" new frontman Papa V Perpetua|magazine=[[Revolver (magazine)|Revolver]]|date=4 March 2025|access-date=26 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250305104228/https://www.revolvermag.com/news/ghost-set-to-reveal-satanized-new-frontman-papa-v-perpetua/|archive-date=5 March 2025|url-status=live}}</ref> All versions of Papa are actually the same vocalist, Tobias Forge.<ref name="Ghost AllMusic"/><ref name="papaivteaser">{{cite web|url=http://www.metalsucks.net/2018/01/19/video-papa-emeritus-iv-listens-to-ghosts-ceremony-and-devotion-on-8-track/|title=Video: Papa Emeritus IV Listens to Ghost's Ceremony and Devotion on 8-Track|work=[[MetalSucks]]|date=19 January 2017|access-date=3 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180203181551/http://www.metalsucks.net/2018/01/19/video-papa-emeritus-iv-listens-to-ghosts-ceremony-and-devotion-on-8-track/|archive-date=3 February 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

Peter Hällje, a former bandmate of former Ghost member Martin Persner, claimed he designed the Papa Emeritus character in 2005, prior to the formation of Ghost. Hällje never performed as Papa Emeritus and agreed with Persner to let him use the character for his then-new band. His claim was later confirmed by Forge.<ref name="forgestatement"/>

=== Cardinal Copia ===
[[File:Ghost - Wacken Open Air 2018-4856.jpg|thumb|right|Cardinal Copia performing in 2018]]
In April 2018, it was revealed that the "new leader" of Ghost would be Cardinal Copia, who made his live debut with the group at a private acoustic show on 6 April; he is not a part of the Papa Emeritus lineage.<ref name="Prequelle"/> Instead, Forge described the situation as "That's why we have a new guy," Forge explains. "The Cardinal is not the boss. He's just the toastmaster. A cardinal is junior to a pope figure. We still have Papa Emeritus [Zero, a.k.a. Papa Nihil] but he's passing on. He needs to teach the Cardinal to become a pope, to earn his skull paint."<ref>{{cite magazine|author=J. Bennett|url=https://www.revolvermag.com/music/ghost-true-story-death-religion-and-rock-roll-behind-metals-strangest-band|title=Ghost: The True Story of Death, Religion and Rock & Roll Behind Metal's Strangest Band|magazine=[[Revolver (magazine)|Revolver]]|date=29 May 2018|access-date=8 September 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180614032856/https://www.revolvermag.com/music/ghost-true-story-death-religion-and-rock-roll-behind-metals-strangest-band/|archive-date=14 June 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

Copia's costume consists of either cardinal vestments or a black or white tuxedo; he also sports a prosthetic mask with black eye makeup and multi-colored eyes, as with the prior Papa Emeritus characters.

In promotion for their 2018 US tour, a video showed that Papa Emeritus one through three had been killed and their bodies embalmed.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Chad|last=Childers|url=http://loudwire.com/ghost-papa-emeritus-i-ii-iii-dead/|title=Ghost's Papa Emeritus I, II & III Are Dead|magazine=[[Loudwire]]|date=30 April 2018|access-date=11 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180502033233/http://loudwire.com/ghost-papa-emeritus-i-ii-iii-dead/|archive-date=2 May 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> In an interview the following month, Forge stated that unlike Ghost's previous frontmen, Cardinal Copia is planned to be around for about five years.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Toni|last=Gonzalez|url=http://loudwire.com/ghost-like-star-wars-tobias-forge-explains/|title=Ghost Are Like 'Star Wars': Tobias Forge Explains|magazine=[[Loudwire]]|date=9 May 2018|access-date=11 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180511225359/http://loudwire.com/ghost-like-star-wars-tobias-forge-explains/|archive-date=11 May 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> The band also welcomed Papa Nihil, the first band member besides Forge to receive a character name. Originally introduced as Papa Emeritus Zero, Nihil is the ancestor of all previous Papa Emeritus characters, and after the "deaths" of his descendants, was the only surviving member of the Papa Emeritus lineage that we know of.<ref name="Guardian2018"/> During the final show of [[A Pale Tour Named Death|the tour in support of ''Prequelle'']], Cardinal Copia was "elevated" to become Papa Emeritus IV.<ref>{{cite web|first=Joe|last=DiVita|url=https://loudwire.com/ghost-papa-emeritus-iv-new-singer/|title=Ghost's Cardinal Copia Out, Papa Emeritus IV Introduced As New Singer|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=4 March 2020|access-date=29 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250305191940/https://loudwire.com/ghost-papa-emeritus-iv-new-singer/|archive-date=5 March 2025|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Identities ===
[[File:Ghost - Austin 2016 5.jpg|thumb|left|The Nameless Ghouls performing in Austin, Texas, 2016]]
Anonymity is a major characteristic of Ghost; prior to 2017, the members had not publicly revealed their names, and the group's five instrumentalists are only referred to as "Nameless Ghouls". During signings, the Nameless Ghouls sign the merchandise by stamping their individual alchemical symbol, while Papa Emeritus signs with his stage name or the letters "P.E."<ref name="reddit"/> One Ghoul said the idea that the band's members remain anonymous to gain attention is a misconception, and that the idea was to remove their personalities to allow their audiences to focus upon the artwork itself. He also said, "Had not the music been rocking, I don't think that people would have gone gaga just about our looks".<ref name="arrival"/> In 2011, a Nameless Ghoul said, "We're often mistaken for roadies, which is helpful. We've almost been thrown out of venues we've played. Forgetting our backstage pass is a big problem."<ref name="Hellbound">{{cite web|author=Justin M. Norton|url=http://www.hellbound.ca/2011/12/ghost-the-hellbound-interview/|title=Ghost: The Hellbound Interview|work=Hell Bound|date=12 December 2011|access-date=10 April 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120110151141/http://www.hellbound.ca/2011/12/ghost-the-hellbound-interview/|archive-date=10 January 2012|url-status=live}}</ref> In early 2012, a member of the band said he enjoyed being an individual and that he could easily "step outside the bubble" when he wanted to.<ref name="bminterview"/> In May 2013, a Ghoul disclosed that they had started to reveal their membership in the group to their local friends and family "for house peace."<ref>{{cite news|first=Scott|last=Mervis|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/ae/music/2013/05/16/Preview-Ghost-B-C-to-haunt-an-old-church/stories/201305160261|title=Preview: Ghost B.C. to haunt an old church|newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]|date=16 May 2013|access-date=17 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151126121807/https://www.post-gazette.com/ae/music/2013/05/16/Preview-Ghost-B-C-to-haunt-an-old-church/stories/201305160261|archive-date=26 November 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>

In an August 2013 interview with [[Jack Osbourne]] for [[Fuse (TV channel)|Fuse News]], a member of the band said that [[Dave Grohl]] has dressed up as a Nameless Ghoul and secretly performed with Ghost.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fuse.tv/videos/2013/08/lollapalooza-2013-ghost-bc-interview|title=Dave Grohl Wears Hooded Robe to Play With Swede Metalheads Ghost B.C.|publisher=[[Fuse (TV channel)|Fuse]]|date=10 August 2013|access-date=30 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250220000236/http://www.fuse.tv/videos/2013/08/lollapalooza-2013-ghost-bc-interview|archive-date=20 February 2025|url-status=live}}</ref> In April 2014, a Nameless Ghoul revealed that the group has had several member changes through the years.<ref>{{cite AV media|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oDkzumtQBmQ|title=Ghost B.C. Interview – Nameless Ghoul|medium=web video|date=28 April 2014|access-date=5 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160419085645/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oDkzumtQBmQ|archive-date=19 April 2016|url-status=dead|time=8:04|publisher=[[Consequence (publication)|Consequence]]|quote=We've changed members through the years actually...}}</ref>

The [[Swedish Performing Rights Society]] was rumored to have Tobias Forge, vocalist of Swedish bands Subvision and [[Repugnant]] and former guitarist for [[Crashdïet]] (using the alias Mary Goore in the latter two), credited with songs as "A Ghoul Writer".<ref>{{cite web|first=Zach|last=Shaw|url=http://www.metalinsider.net/mystery-solved/ghost-frontman%E2%80%99s-identity-revealed|title=Ghost Frontman's Identity Revealed Tobias Forge|work=Metal Insider|date=22 August 2011|access-date=30 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811095956/http://www.metalinsider.net/mystery-solved/ghost-frontman%E2%80%99s-identity-revealed|archive-date=11 August 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> All of the band's songs are credited to "A Ghoul Writer", causing people to suspect that Forge was Papa Emeritus. The online database for US-based performance rights society ASCAP, when having the name Tobias Forge entered into its search box, revealed all of Ghost's original songs (even though many of the tracks use the pseudonym "A Ghoul Writer" in the database itself)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ascap.com/ace/#ace/writer/293703355/FORGE%20TOBIAS%20JENS|title=ASCAP database of all songs written by Tobias Forge/A Ghoul Writer|publisher=[[American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers|ASCAP]]|access-date=21 October 2018}}</ref>  At the time, Ghost stated they would not comment on any rumors of their identities.<ref name="bminterview"/> Following a lawsuit in 2017, Forge's identity as Papa Emeritus was revealed.<ref name="lawsuit"/>

In March 2017, Swedish musician Martin Persner of the band [[Magna Carta Cartel]] claimed in a short video clip that he was the rhythm guitarist, also known as Omega, from 2009 to July 2016. This marked the first time that someone has publicly identified themselves as a member of Ghost.<ref name="Persner">{{cite web|first=Robert|last=Pasbani|url=http://www.metalinjection.net/latest-news/breakups/former-ghost-nameless-ghoul-reveals-himself-to-be-swedish-musician-martin-persner|title=Former Ghost Nameless Ghoul Reveals Himself To Be Swedish Musician Martin Persner|work=Metal Injection|date=2 March 2017|access-date=30 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180307230957/http://www.metalinjection.net/latest-news/breakups/former-ghost-nameless-ghoul-reveals-himself-to-be-swedish-musician-martin-persner|archive-date=7 March 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> A few months before Persner's announcement, the band recruited a new bass player who was suspected to be [[Lez Zeppelin]] bassist Megan Thomas, later confirmed by Forge.<ref name="forgestatement"/><ref>{{cite web|first=Greg|last=Kennelty|url=http://www.metalinjection.net/shocking-revelations/the-internet-has-figured-out-who-ghosts-female-bassist-is|title=The Internet Has Figured Out Who Ghost's Female Bassist Is|work=Metal Injection|date=26 September 2016|access-date=30 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240524101858/http://www.metalinjection.net/shocking-revelations/the-internet-has-figured-out-who-ghosts-female-bassist-is|archive-date=24 May 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> A lawsuit against Forge in April 2017 on behalf of four past members revealed their names, as well as the names of several more past members.<ref name="lawsuitmembers"/> When asked about the complete lineup change at the end of 2016, Forge stated that Ghost "was always sort of... I guess a [[Bathory (band)|Bathory]] sort of band, where there was people playing live, and the people playing live [were] not necessarily the same that played on the records."<ref name="forgeinterview">{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/tobias-forge-a-k-a-papa-emeritus-ghost-was-never-formed-as-a-band/|title=Tobias Forge (a.k.a. Papa Emeritus): 'Ghost Was Never Formed As A Band'|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=22 April 2017|access-date=19 May 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170425003917/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/tobias-forge-a-k-a-papa-emeritus-ghost-was-never-formed-as-a-band/|archive-date=25 April 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> The lawsuit was dismissed by the court on 17 October 2018.<ref name="dismissal">{{cite web|first=Greg|last=Kennelty|url=https://metalinjection.net/its-just-business/lawsuit-against-ghost-frontman-by-ex-band-dismissed-by-swedish-court|title=Lawsuit Against Ghost Frontman By Ex-Band Dismissed By Swedish Court|work=Metal Injection|date=17 October 2018|access-date=30 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241130090251/https://metalinjection.net/its-just-business/lawsuit-against-ghost-frontman-by-ex-band-dismissed-by-swedish-court|archive-date=30 November 2024|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Timeline===
====Stage names / Character identities====
As a band with a unique and complex theatrical presentation,<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Merlin|last=Alderslade|url=https://www.loudersound.com/features/the-ghost-family-tree|title=Ghost: the definitive guide to every member of their crazy universe|magazine=[[Metal Hammer]]|date=8 March 2022|access-date=24 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220308080529/https://www.loudersound.com/features/the-ghost-family-tree|archive-date=8 March 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> the musicians in Ghost's live performances do not perform as themselves, but each play a character. Emphasis is placed on the singer, currently "Papa V Perpetua".<ref>{{cite web|first=Bryan|last=Rolli|url=https://loudwire.com/ghost-perpetua-meaning/|title=What Is the Meaning of Perpetua, Name of Ghost's New Frontman?|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=5 March 2025|access-date=31 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250305214304/https://loudwire.com/ghost-perpetua-meaning/|archive-date=5 March 2025|url-status=live}}</ref> The rest of the band are officially deemed "Nameless Ghouls"<ref>{{cite web|first=Joe|last=DiVita|url=https://loudwire.com/ghosts-current-nameless-ghouls-have-been-identified-see-unmasked-photo/|title=Ghost's Current Nameless Ghouls Have Been Identified, See Unmasked Photo|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=20 May 2022|access-date=31 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250218042722/https://loudwire.com/ghosts-current-nameless-ghouls-have-been-identified-see-unmasked-photo/|archive-date=18 February 2025|url-status=live}}</ref> but there are general categories based on the roles of each of the "ghouls". The five [[classical element]]s of fire, earth, water, air, and aether were originally used to identify the ghouls<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Kyle|last=McGovern|url=https://www.spin.com/2013/04/ghost-bc-reddit-ama-infestissumam-secret-identities/|title=Members of Ghost B.C. Keep Identities Secret Through Bribes|magazine=[[Spin (magazine)|Spin]]|date=16 April 2013|access-date=31 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240413065335/https://www.spin.com/2013/04/ghost-bc-reddit-ama-infestissumam-secret-identities/|archive-date=13 April 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> with symbol patches on each ghoul's stage outfit,{{CN|date=March 2025}} but with the touring cycle coinciding with the 2018 release of ''[[Prequelle]]'', the live lineup expanded to include 7 ghouls, and thus the elemental symbols were no longer displayed or officially used.{{CN|date=March 2025}}

As a general rule, Ghost does not directly identify any of the ghouls through their official accounts or spokespeople, but in recent years, they have become more relaxed in allowing this information to become public.<ref>{{cite web|first=Joe|last=DiVita|url=https://loudwire.com/ghosts-current-nameless-ghouls-have-been-identified-see-unmasked-photo/|title=Ghost's Current Nameless Ghouls Have Been Identified, See Unmasked Photo|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=20 May 2022|access-date=24 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220520134319/https://loudwire.com/ghosts-current-nameless-ghouls-have-been-identified-see-unmasked-photo/|archive-date=20 May 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="blab22id">{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/ghosts-imperatour-nameless-ghouls-identified-unmasked-photo-available|title=Ghost's 'Imperatour' Nameless Ghouls Identified; 'Unmasked' Photo Available|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=19 May 2022|access-date=24 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220519222840/https://blabbermouth.net/news/ghosts-imperatour-nameless-ghouls-identified-unmasked-photo-available|archive-date=19 May 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Robert|last=Pasbani|url=https://metalinjection.net/news/breakups/former-ghost-nameless-ghoul-reveals-himself-to-be-swedish-musician-martin-persner|title=Former Ghost Nameless Ghoul Reveals Himself To Be Swedish Musician Martin Persner|work=Metal Injection|date=2 March 2017|access-date=24 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201025064447/https://metalinjection.net/news/breakups/former-ghost-nameless-ghoul-reveals-himself-to-be-swedish-musician-martin-persner|archive-date=25 October 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Robert|last=Pasbani|url=https://metalinjection.net/metal-crimes/former-nameless-ghoul-explains-lawsuit-against-ghosts-papa-emeritus-reveals-other-former-ghouls-identity|title=Former Nameless Ghoul Explains Lawsuit Against Ghost's Papa Emeritus, Reveals Other Former Ghouls' Identity|work=Metal Injection|date=6 April 2017|access-date=24 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170406215520/https://metalinjection.net/metal-crimes/former-nameless-ghoul-explains-lawsuit-against-ghosts-papa-emeritus-reveals-other-former-ghouls-identity|archive-date=6 April 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> Because of the band's long-standing practice of using [[Non-disclosure agreement|NDAs]],<ref>{{cite magazine|author=J. Bennett|url=https://www.revolvermag.com/music/ghost-true-story-death-religion-and-rock-roll-behind-metals-strangest-band|title=Ghost: The True Story of Death, Religion and Rock & Roll Behind Metal's Strangest Band|magazine=[[Revolver (magazine)|Revolver]]|date=29 May 2018|access-date=24 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180529191735/https://www.revolvermag.com/music/ghost-true-story-death-religion-and-rock-roll-behind-metals-strangest-band|archive-date=29 May 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> the ghouls are not allowed to discuss their involvement in the band publicly while they are active members, though the avid fanbase tends to deduce the ghouls' identities rather quickly once they've appeared on stage.{{CN|date=March 2025}}

'''Volbeat''' are<!-- Please refer to WP:ENGVAR. This article is written in British English, which uses the plural format while referring to music groups. Volbeat may also refer to a Pokémon, but is completely different. Please do NOT change "are" to "is". Thank you. --> a Danish [[Rock music|rock]] band formed in [[Copenhagen]] in 2001. They play a fusion of [[rock and roll]] and [[Heavy metal music|heavy metal]]. Their current line-up consists of vocalist and rhythm guitarist [[Michael Poulsen]], drummer [[Jon Larsen (Danish musician)|Jon Larsen]], and bassist Kaspar Boye Larsen. The band is signed to Dutch label Mascot Records and has released nine studio albums and one DVD. Their second album ''[[Rock the Rebel/Metal the Devil]]'' received platinum status, and their 2010 release ''[[Beyond Hell/Above Heaven]]'' was subject to widespread international critical acclaim, receiving triple platinum in Denmark and Austria, double platinum in Sweden, platinum in Canada, 5× Gold in Germany, and gold in both Finland and the United States.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.riaa.com/gold-platinum/?tab_active=default-award&se=volbeat#search_section|title=Gold & Platinum - RIAA|work=RIAA|access-date=18 March 2017}}</ref> Volbeat's most recent studio album,  ''[[God of Angels Trust]]'', was released in 2025.

==History==

===Early years (2001–2009)===
[[File:Volbeat Michael Poulsen 2009.jpg|thumb|left|Michael Poulsen, lead singer, rhythm guitarist and main songwriter of Volbeat]]
Singer [[Michael Poulsen]]'s first band was [[death metal]] act, [[Dominus (band)|Dominus]].<ref name="katt">{{cite web|url=http://www.katt.com/2014/04/22/jake-daniels-tuesdays-broadcast-4-22-14/|title=Jake Daniels Tuesday's Broadcast 4-22-17|date=22 April 2014|access-date=16 September 2014}}</ref><ref name="allmusic1">{{cite web|last=True|first=Chris|url=https://www.allmusic.com/artist/volbeat-mn0000725175/biography|title=Volbeat Biography|publisher=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=16 September 2019}}</ref> In 2000, Poulsen became fed up with the death metal music scene, causing Dominus to break up.<ref name="allmusic1"/><ref name="katt"/> In 2001, Poulsen went on to form a new band with some friends and other former Dominus members.<ref name="allmusic1"/> This was the beginning of Volbeat.<ref name="allmusic1"/>

The band name "Volbeat" was derived from Dominus's third album name, ''Vol.Beat'' (read as: Volume Beat).<ref name="katt"/> After selling 1,000 copies of their ''Beat the Meat'' demo tape, Volbeat was signed to a record deal by Rebel Monster Records, a sub-label of Mascot Records.<ref name="allmusic1"/>

Volbeat released their first album, ''[[The Strength/The Sound/The Songs]]'' in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.discogs.com/Volbeat-The-Strength-The-Sound-The-Songs/release/955581|title=Volbeat - The Strength / The Sound / The Songs|website=Discogs|language=en|access-date=25 January 2017}}</ref> The line-up for the album consisted of Michael Poulsen (vocals), Jon Larsen (drums), Franz Gottschalk (guitar) and Anders Kjølholm (bass).<ref name="allmusic1"/> The album was a huge success in Denmark achieving a spot at No. 18 in the charts.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.metalstorm.ee/bands/biography.php?band_id=2788&bandname=Volbeat |title=Volbeat - Biography - Metal Storm |publisher=MetalStorm.ee |access-date=20 February 2010 |archive-date=24 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190924155649/http://www.metalstorm.net/bands/biography.php?band_id=2788&bandname=Volbeat |url-status=dead }}</ref> Critics were generally positive towards ''The Strength / The Sound / The Songs''. The German [[hard rock]] magazine RockHard gave it 10/10 in a review.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rockhard.de/index.php?smod=p209Wz1iMUIfo2qAo2D9pz9wn2uupzDhpzI2nJI3pl5xMKEunJkJnJI3Wzqlo3IjFHD9pzuspzI2nJI3WzAioaEyoaEWEQ00ZQV4AlMmqJAbp3ElnJ5aCKMioTWyLKDz |title=Rock Hard Online rockt das Web |publisher=RockHard.de |access-date=20 February 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927235922/http://www.rockhard.de/index.php?smod=p209Wz1iMUIfo2qAo2D9pz9wn2uupzDhpzI2nJI3pl5xMKEunJkJnJI3Wzqlo3IjFHD9pzuspzI2nJI3WzAioaEyoaEWEQ00ZQV4AlMmqJAbp3ElnJ5aCKMioTWyLKDz |archive-date=27 September 2007 |url-status=dead  }}</ref> ''The Strength / The Sound / The Songs'' also received a handful of awards, including Best Album in the Danish Metal Musik Awards in 2005.{{citation needed|date=May 2022}} Volbeat was praised for its [[concert|live performance]]s. Their concert at [[Roskilde Festival]] 2006 received a 6/6 stars review in the Danish newspaper [[B.T. (tabloid)|BT]].{{citation needed|date=May 2022}}

[[File:20140613-067-Nova Rock 2014-Volbeat-Anders Kjølholm.JPG|thumb|right|upright=0.6|Bassist Anders Kjølholm at [[Nova Rock Festival|Nova Rock]] 2014]]
The band released their second album, ''[[Rock the Rebel/Metal the Devil]]'', in week 8 of 2007; it debuted as No. 1 in the Danish Top 40 for CD-sales.{{citation needed|date=May 2022}}

They opened the [[Roskilde Festival]] in 2007 and also supported [[Metallica]] together with [[Mnemic]] at their concert in Denmark 13 July of that year.<ref name="allmusic1"/> They supported [[Megadeth]] in Finland and in their home town, [[Copenhagen]], and made a few festival appearances mid-2008.<ref name="allmusic1"/> They hired [[Thomas Bredahl]] following the recording of ''Rock the Rebel / Metal the Devil'' as a replacement for Gottschalk on guitar.<ref name="allmusic1"/>

In 2008, Volbeat released their third album, ''[[Guitar Gangsters & Cadillac Blood]]'' featuring guitarist Thomas Bredahl. It topped the Finnish Album Chart straight after its publication.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://yle.fi/lista/listat/tuote.php?id=8898 |title=Suomen virallinen lista |publisher=yle.fi |access-date=16 July 2009 |archive-date=26 September 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080926223400/http://yle.fi/lista/listat/tuote.php?id=8898 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2009, Volbeat supported the symphonic metal band [[Nightwish]] on their U.S. tour in May.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.metalfromfinland.com/news/2008-10-28_23:47/volbeat_to_support_nightwish_on_spring_2009_us_tour |title=Volbeat To Support Nightwish on Spring 2009 U.S. Tour - Metal from Finland |publisher=MetalFromFinland.com |date=28 October 2008 |access-date=20 February 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120220013008/http://www.metalfromfinland.com/news/2008-10-28_23:47/volbeat_to_support_nightwish_on_spring_2009_us_tour |archive-date=20 February 2012 |url-status=dead  }}</ref> On 31 May 2009 they were on the main stage of the [[Pinkpop Festival]]. They also supported Metallica on the North American leg of Metallica's [[World Magnetic Tour]] from October to December 2009.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.metallica.com/index.asp?item=602410 |title=Metallica.com - More Opening Act News |publisher=Metallica.com |date=27 July 2009 |access-date=20 February 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100125041505/http://www.metallica.com/index.asp?item=602410 |archive-date=25 January 2010 |url-status=dead  }}</ref>
In 2009 the band played at the biggest open-air festival in Europe (400,000–500,000 rock fans every year), [[Przystanek Woodstock]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.en.wosp.org.pl/woodstock/|title=Home - Wielka Orkiestra Świątecznej Pomocy|work=Wielka Orkiestra Swiątecznej Pomocy|access-date=10 January 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100325213029/http://www.en.wosp.org.pl/woodstock/|archive-date=25 March 2010}}</ref> in Poland.

=== Line-up changes (2010–2015) ===
[[File:20140613-064-Nova_Rock_2014-Volbeat-Michael_Schøn_Poulsen_and_Rob_Caggiano.JPG|thumb|right|Rob Caggiano and Michael Poulsen at [[Nova Rock Festival|Nova Rock]] 2014]]

In June 2010, Volbeat performed at [[Download Festival]] .<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rocksound.tv/news/read/download-2010-stage-times-revealed|title=Download 2010 Stage Times Revealed|publisher=Rock Sound|date=8 June 2018|access-date=16 September 2019}}</ref> and also joined [[Metallica]], [[Megadeth]], [[Anthrax (American band)|Anthrax]], [[Slayer]] and others in the "Big Four" show at Sonisphere Switzerland.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://sz.sonispherefestivals.com/2010/01/volbeat-definitiv-bestatigt/ |title=VOLBEAT DEFINITIV BESTÄTIGT: Sonisphere 2010 Switzerland |publisher=SonisphereFestivals.com |date=10 January 2010 |access-date=20 February 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100724130615/http://sz.sonispherefestivals.com/2010/01/volbeat-definitiv-bestatigt/ |archive-date=24 July 2010 |url-status=dead  }}</ref> 

The new album, ''[[Beyond Hell/Above Heaven]]'' was released on 10 September 2010. Poulsen said the title "refers to the overall theme of the album, and it continues the storyline from where ''Guitar Gangsters & Cadillac Blood'' left off...".<ref name=voldk>{{cite web |url=http://volbeat.dk/2010/02/15/volbeat-reveals-album-title/ |title=Volbeat: Official Homepage - Volbeat Reveals Album Title! |publisher=Volbeat.dk |date=15 February 2010 |access-date=20 February 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100222225514/http://volbeat.dk/2010/02/15/volbeat-reveals-album-title/ |archive-date=22 February 2010 }}</ref> The album was supported by a tour in November.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://volbeat.dk/2010/05/14/album-release-and-fall-dates-confirmed/ |title=Volbeat: Official Homepage - Album release and fall dates confirmed! |publisher=Volbeat.dk |date=14 May 2010 |access-date=30 May 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100521131137/http://volbeat.dk/2010/05/14/album-release-and-fall-dates-confirmed/ |archive-date=21 May 2010 |url-status=dead  }}</ref> 

Volbeat's 2011 Grand Summer Tour across North America began in Toronto, Ontario on 24 July at Heavy T.O., and concluded with a two-night stand on 3 & 4 September at the House of Blues in Anaheim, CA. Volbeat co-headlined this tour with rock powerhouse [[Cold (band)|Cold]] on all US dates, but not in Canada. On 28 November 2011, Bredahl departed the band.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.volbeat.dk/2/news.php?id=70&lang=en |title=Under Construction |publisher=Volbeat.dk |access-date=20 September 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120429015255/http://www.volbeat.dk/2/news.php?id=70&lang=en |archive-date=29 April 2012 |url-status=dead  }}</ref> Volbeat committed to playing all 2011–2012 as scheduled either as a trio, or with a replacement guitarist. On 26 January 2012, Volbeat joined [[Megadeth]], [[Motörhead]], and [[Lacuna Coil]] on [[Gigantour]]. The tour started in Camden, New Jersey, and culminated on 28 February 2012 in Denver, Colorado, at The Fillmore Auditorium. On the tour, Hank Shermann ([[Mercyful Fate]]) filled in as the guitarist for Volbeat. On their North American Summer tour, which began in June 2012, [[Iced Earth]] and [[Hellyeah]] were the supporting acts. The tour included dates in Baltimore, Toronto, Detroit, Billings, Boston, Tempe, San Francisco, and Weyburn and Lazerfest in Boone, Iowa, and in June, Orion Music Festival, headlined by Metallica, at Bader Field in Atlantic City, New Jersey.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://lineup.orionmusicandmore.com/events/2012/06/23/ |title=Orion Music + More 2013 |publisher=Lineup.orionmusicandmore.com |access-date=20 September 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130225102702/http://lineup.orionmusicandmore.com/events/2012/06/23/ |archive-date=25 February 2013 |url-status=dead  }}</ref>

[[File:Volbeat 2013.jpg|thumb|left|Volbeat performing in 2013]]

In February 2013, Rob Caggiano, formerly of [[Anthrax (American band)|Anthrax]], joined the band as second guitarist.<ref>{{cite web|first=Vince|last=Neilstein|url=https://www.metalsucks.net/2013/02/04/ex-anthrax-guitarist-rob-caggiano-joins-volbeat/|title=Ex-Anthrax Guitarist Rob Caggiano Joins… Volbeat?!|work=[[MetalSucks]]|date=4 February 2013|access-date=16 January 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.guitarworld.com/news/former-anthrax-axeman-rob-caggiano-joins-volbeat-second-guitarist|title=Former Anthrax Axeman Rob Caggiano Joins Volbeat as Second Guitarist|work=[[Guitar World]]|date=4 February 2013|access-date=16 January 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Graham|last=Hartmann|url=https://loudwire.com/volbeat-welcome-former-anthrax-guitarist-rob-caggiano-reveal-details-new-album/|title=Volbeat Welcome Former Anthrax Guitarist Rob Caggiano Into Band, Reveal Details For New Album|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=4 February 2013|access-date=16 January 2023}}</ref> He had been producing and recording guest solos on the band's upcoming album, ''[[Outlaw Gentlemen & Shady Ladies]]'', before being asked to join as a full-time member. Singer and guitarist [[Michael Poulsen]] called the collaboration between Caggiano and the rest of the band "so inspiring and in good spirit that we the decided to keep him. Basically we went into the studio as a three piece and came out as a whole band!"<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.volbeat.dk/2/news.php?id=98&lang=en |title=Under Construction |publisher=Volbeat.dk |access-date=20 September 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130208043040/http://www.volbeat.dk/2/news.php?id=98&lang=en |archive-date=8 February 2013 }}</ref> The album, ''Outlaw Gentlemen & Shady Ladies'', was released in April 2013.<ref name="allmusic1"/>

Volbeat toured with [[Danko Jones]] and [[Spoken (band)|Spoken]] in spring 2013{{fact|date=July 2025}} and played at the Download festival in June 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theprp.com/2012/12/03/news/coal-chamber-set-for-2013-download-festival/|title=Coal Chamber Set For 2013 "Download Festival"|work=The PRP|date=3 December 2012|access-date=16 January 2023}}</ref> 

In 2015, the band worked on a new album, with a new song demoed throughout "The Devil's Bleeding Crown" tour.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/volbeat-performs-new-song-at-san-antonios-river-city-rockfest-video/|title=Video: Volbeat Performs New Song|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=25 May 2015|access-date=22 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Chad|last=Childers|url=https://loudwire.com/volbeat-anthrax-crobot-2015-tour/|title=Volbeat Taking Anthrax + Crobot on 2015 Tour|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=27 October 2014|access-date=16 January 2023}}</ref>

In November 2015, Kjølholm left Volbeat on, as both sides emphasised, good terms with the band.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/volbeat-parts-ways-with-bassist-anders-kjolholm/|title=Volbeat Parts Ways With Bassist Anders Kjølholm|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=13 November 2015|access-date=9 December 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://metalinjection.net/news/breakups/volbeat-part-ways-with-bassist-anders-kjolholm|title=Volbeat Part Ways With Bassist Anders Kjølholm|work=Metal Injection|date=13 November 2015|access-date=15 January 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Chad|last=Childers|url=https://loudwire.com/volbeat-part-ways-bassist-anders-kjolholm/|title=Volbeat Part Ways With Bassist Anders Kjolholm|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=13 November 2015|access-date=15 January 2023}}</ref>

=== Recent works (2016–present) ===

In April 2016, "The Devil's Bleeding Crown" was released as the first single from the upcoming album, ''Seal the Deal and Let's Boogie''.<ref name="2016album"/><ref>{{cite web|first=Martin|last=Kielty|url=https://www.loudersound.com/news/volbeat-video-devils-bleeding-crown-6th-album-seal-the-deal-lets-boogie|title=Volbeat premiere The Devil's Bleeding Crown|work=[[Classic Rock (magazine)|Classic Rock]]|date=8 April 2016|access-date=15 January 2023}}</ref> A second single,  "For Evigt" (Forever), and an English version, "The Bliss", were released 29 April.<ref>{{cite web|first=Robert|last=Pasbani|url=http://www.metalinjection.net/latest-news/volbeat-release-two-versions-of-brand-new-track-the-bliss|title=Volbeat Release Two Versions of Brand New Track "The Bliss," So Catchy It Will Get Stuck In Your Head|work=Metal Injection|date=29 April 2016|access-date=1 May 2017}}</ref> The album was released on 3 June 2016.<ref name="2016album">{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/volbeat-to-release-seal-the-deal-listen-to-first-single-the-devils-bleeding-crown/|title=Volbeat's 'Seal The Deal & Let's Boogie' Album Due in June; Listen To 'The Devil's Bleeding Crown' Single|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=7 April 2016|access-date=8 April 2016}}</ref>

On 2 June 2021, the band released two singles, "Wait a Minute My Girl" and "Dagen Før", the latter featuring [[Alphabeat]]'s Stine Bramsen.<ref>{{cite web |title=Volbeat Debuts Two New Songs For The Summer, 'Wait A Minute My Girl' And 'Dagen Før'|url=https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/volbeat-debuts-two-new-songs-for-the-summer-wait-a-minute-my-girl-and-dagen-for/|website=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=2 June 2021|access-date=2 June 2021}}</ref> "Wait a Minute My Girl" earned the band their ninth No. 1 on ''Billboard''{{'}}s Mainstream Rock Airplay chart dated for 21 August 2021. 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Chad|last=Childers|url=https://loudwire.com/volbeat-becoming-lyrics-video/|title=Volbeat Unveil Thrashy + Anthemic New Song 'Becoming'|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=23 September 2021|access-date=28 October 2021}}</ref> The album, ''[[Servant of the Mind]]'', was released on 3 December 2021.<ref name=SGB/>

In early 2022 Volbeat co-headlined a tour with [[Ghost (Swedish band)|Ghost]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Emily|last=Carter|url=https://www.kerrang.com/ghost-and-volbeat-announce-2022-u-s-co-headline-tour|title=Ghost and Volbeat announce 2022 U.S. co-headline tour|work=[[Kerrang!]]|date=20 September 2021|access-date=14 January 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Chad|last=Childers|url=https://loudwire.com/ghost-volbeat-2022-us-co-headline-tour-dates/|title=Ghost + Volbeat Announce 2022 U.S. Co-Headline Tour Dates|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=20 September 2021|access-date=12 December 2021}}</ref> When the band's drummer, [[Jon Larsen (Danish musician)|Jon Larsen]], was tested positive for [[COVID-19]] in January 2022, the band had to cancel one show but continued the tour, with [[Slayer]]'s former drummer, [[Jon Dette]], filling in as a touring drummer until Larsen's return.<ref name="Jon Dette 1">{{cite web|url=https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/volbeats-jon-larsen-tests-positive-for-covid-19-ex-slayer-drummer-jon-dette-to-fill-in/|title=Volbeat's Jon Larsen Tests Positive For COVID-19; Ex-Slayer Drummer Jon Dette To Fill In|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=28 January 2022|access-date=28 January 2022}}</ref><ref name="Jon Dette 2">{{cite web|url=https://www.wirx.com/2022/01/28/volbeat-drops-off-show-with-ghost-after-drummer-tests-positive-for-covid-19/|title=Volbeat Drops Off Show With Ghost After Drummer Tests Positive For Covid-19|work=[[WIRX]]|date=28 January 2022|access-date=28 January 2022}}</ref> On 13 April 2022, the band released a music video for the song "Temple of Ekur".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/volbeat-releases-music-video-for-temple-of-ekur|title=Volbeat Releases Music Video For 'Temple Of Ekur'|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=13 April 2022|access-date=14 January 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://bravewords.com/news/volbeat-debut-temple-of-ekur-music-video|title=Volbeat Debut "Temple Of Ekur" Music Video|work=[[Brave Words & Bloody Knuckles|Brave Words]]|date=13 April 2022|access-date=13 April 2022|archive-date=13 April 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220413222046/https://bravewords.com/news/volbeat-debut-temple-of-ekur-music-video|url-status=dead}}</ref> 

On 5 June 2023, Volbeat parted ways with lead guitarist Rob Caggiano. For the band's Summer 2023 tour, the lead guitarist position was filled by Flemming C. Lund of The Arcane Order.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/volbeat-parts-ways-with-guitarist-rob-caggiano|title=Volbeat Parts Ways With Guitarist|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=5 June 2023|access-date=5 June 2023}}</ref> 

In 2024, the band members spent time at home and also worked on a new album, scheduled for release in 2025. Michael Poulsen also went on tour with his new death metal band, Asinhell.<ref>{{cite web|first=Chad|last=Childers|url=https://loudwire.com/volbeat-michael-poulsen-2024-update/|title=Volbeat's Michael Poulsen Lays Out Band's Plan for 2024|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=24 August 2023|access-date=18 September 2023}}</ref> 

2025 saw the release of the singles "By a Monster’s Hand" (6 March),<ref name=Monster>{{cite web|first=Joe|last=DiVita|url=https://loudwire.com/volbeat-god-of-angels-trust-by-a-monsters-hand-2025-tour/|title=Volbeat Announce 9th Album, Debut Heavy New Song + Book Giant 2025 Tour|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=6 March 2025|access-date=6 March 2025}}</ref> "In the Barn of the Goat Giving Birth to Satan's Spawn in a Dying World of Doom" (4 April),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/volbeat-shares-new-single-in-the-barn-of-the-goat-giving-birth-to-satans-spawn-in-a-dying-world-of-doom#google_vignette|title=Volbeat Shares New Single 'In the Barn of the Goat Giving Birth to Satan's Spawn in a Dying World of Doom'|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=4 April 2025|access-date=4 April 2025}}</ref> "Time Will Heal" (16 May)<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Gregory|last=Adams|url=https://www.revolvermag.com/music/hear-volbeats-tender-new-rocker-time-will-heal/|title=Hear Volbeat's tender new rocker "Time Will Heal"|magazine=[[Revolver (magazine)|Revolver]]|date=16 May 2025|access-date=16 May 2025}}</ref> ahead of their ninth studio album, ''[[God of Angels Trust]]'', released on 6 June 2025.<ref name=Monster/>

==Musical style and influences==
Volbeat is noted for having a "novel take on [[heavy metal music|heavy metal]], infused with straightforward [[rock music|rock]] and [[pop music|pop]] melodies, as well as a peculiar penchant for vintage ‘50s [[rock and roll|rock & roll]]".<ref name="Loudwire genres2">{{cite web|first=Dustin|last=Schoof|url=https://loudwire.com/tags/volbeat/|title=Volbeat|work=[[Loudwire]]|access-date=14 January 2023}}</ref> Chris True of [[AllMusic]] stated, "[the band's] sound weds [[hard rock]], classic metal, glam, [[Punk rock|punk]], and [[rockabilly]]."<ref name="allmusic1"/> Their influences encompass 1950s rockabilly, [[country music|country]] and pop, as well as heavy metal and hard rock of the 1970s and '80s.<ref name="lehighvalleylive"/> These influences include [[Elvis Presley]], [[Johnny Cash]], [[Metallica]], [[Black Sabbath]], [[Obituary (band)|Obituary]], [[Mercyful Fate]], [[Darkthrone]], [[Mayhem (band)|Mayhem]], [[King Diamond (band)|King Diamond]], [[Dio (band)|Dio]], [[Iced Earth]], [[Death (metal band)|Death]], [[Armored Saint]], [[Iron Maiden]], [[Judas Priest]], [[Accept (band)|Accept]], [[Cannibal Corpse]], [[Manowar]], [[AC/DC]], and [[Social Distortion]].<ref name="allmusic1"/> ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' called Volbeat "[[hard rock|hard-rock]]’s preeminent [[psychobilly]] freight train".<ref name="Billboard genres">{{cite magazine|first=Bobby|last=Olivier|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/volbeat-michael-poulsen-interview-new-album-8525785/|title=Volbeat Frontman Michael Poulsen Talks New Album, New Daughter and How a Sea Monster Can Save the World|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=1 August 2019|access-date=16 December 2021}}</ref>  They were also described as "heavy rockabilly"<ref>{{cite web|first=Spencer|last=Kaufman|url=https://consequence.net/2021/06/volbeat-wait-a-minute-my-girl-dagen-for/|title=Volbeat Return with New Songs "Wait a Minute My Girl" and "Dagen Før": Stream|work=[[Consequence (publication)|Consequence]]|date=2 June 2021|access-date=13 April 2022}}</ref> and "[[groove metal]] meets rockabilly".<ref name="loudwire genres">{{cite web|first=Tree|last=Riddle|url=https://loudwire.com/volbeat-announce-2012-north-american-tour-dates-with-hellyeah/|title=Volbeat Announce 2012 North American Tour Dates With HellYeah|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=18 April 2012|access-date=13 April 2022}}</ref> ''Lehigh Valley Live'' described them as a hard rock and heavy metal band.<ref name="lehighvalleylive">{{cite web|first=Dustin|last=Schoof|url=https://www.lehighvalleylive.com/music/index.ssf/2014/04/volbeat_singer_discusses_fan_a.html|title=Volbeat singer discusses fan appreciation, influences and Young the Giant|work=Lehigh Valley Live|date=25 April 2014|access-date=3 July 2018}}</ref>

'''Christopher John Cornell''' ({{né}} '''Boyle'''; July 20, 1964&nbsp;– May 18, 2017) was an American musician, best known as the lead vocalist, rhythm guitarist, and the primary lyricist for the [[rock music|rock]] bands [[Soundgarden]] and [[Audioslave]]. He also had a solo career and contributed to numerous movie soundtracks. Cornell was the founder and frontman of [[Temple of the Dog]], a one-off tribute band dedicated to his late friend, musician [[Andrew Wood (singer)|Andrew Wood]]. Several music journalists, fan polls and fellow musicians have regarded Cornell as one of the greatest rock singers of all time.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chris Cornell had one of rock's great voices – and one of its most curious minds |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=May 18, 2017 |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/music/la-et-ms-chris-cornell-appreciation-20170518-story.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170518205704/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/music/la-et-ms-chris-cornell-appreciation-20170518-story.html|archive-date=May 18, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Pearl Jam's Stone Gossard: Chris Cornell is the GOAT |date=December 17, 2022 |url=https://www.loudersound.com/news/pearl-jams-stone-gossard-chris-cornell-is-the-goat|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221217082502/https://www.loudersound.com/news/pearl-jams-stone-gossard-chris-cornell-is-the-goat|archive-date=December 17, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>

Cornell is considered a key figure of the 1990s [[grunge]] movement with an extensive songwriting history, a nearly four-[[octave]] vocal range<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.usatoday.com/life/music/news/2009-03-23-cornell-scream_N.htm |title=Chris Cornell takes another sonic shift with 'Scream' |work=[[USA Today]] |author=Gundersen, Edna |access-date=April 29, 2009 |date=March 24, 2009 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090327143114/http://www.usatoday.com/life/music/news/2009-03-23-cornell-scream_N.htm |archive-date=March 27, 2009 }}</ref> and a powerful [[Belting (music)|vocal belting]] technique. Cornell released four solo studio albums, ''[[Euphoria Morning]]'' (1999), ''[[Carry On (Chris Cornell album)|Carry On]]'' (2007), ''[[Scream (Chris Cornell album)|Scream]]'' (2009), and ''[[Higher Truth]]'' (2015); the live album ''[[Songbook (Chris Cornell album)|Songbook]]'' (2011); and two compilations, ''[[The Roads We Choose – A Retrospective|The Roads We Choose]]'' (2007) and ''[[Chris Cornell (album)|Chris Cornell]]'' (2018), the latter released posthumously. He received a [[Golden Globe Award]] nomination for his song "The Keeper", which appeared in the 2011 film ''[[Machine Gun Preacher]]'', and co-wrote and performed "[[You Know My Name]]", the theme song to the 2006 [[James Bond]] film ''[[Casino Royale (2006 film)|Casino Royale]]''. His last solo release before his death was the charity single "[[The Promise (Chris Cornell song)|The Promise]]", written for the ending credits for the 2016 [[The Promise (2016 film)|film of the same name]].

Cornell struggled with [[Major depressive disorder|depression]] for most of his life. He was found dead in his [[Detroit]] hotel room in the early hours of May 18, 2017, after performing at a Soundgarden concert an hour earlier at the [[Fox Theatre (Detroit)|Fox Theatre]]. His death was ruled a [[suicide by hanging]].<ref name="catalog"/>

Cornell sold 14.8 million albums, 8.8 million digital songs, and 300 million on-demand audio streams in the U.S. alone,<ref name="catalog"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.allaccess.com/net-news/archive/story/165844/chris-cornell-dead-at-52-radio-reacts |title=Chris Cornell Dead At 52, Radio Reacts |website=AllAccess.com |date=May 18, 2017 |access-date=May 26, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201042009/https://www.allaccess.com/net-news/archive/story/165844/chris-cornell-dead-at-52-radio-reacts |archive-date=December 1, 2017}}</ref> as well as over 30 million records worldwide.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iheart.com/news/18-things-you-might-not-have-15842434/|title=18 Things You Might Not Have Known About Chris Cornell|website=iHeartRadio|date=May 18, 2017|access-date=May 29, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170518165029/https://www.iheart.com/news/18-things-you-might-not-have-15842434/|archive-date=May 18, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite 21, 2015 |access-date=May 29, 2017}}</ref> Nominated for 18 [[Grammy Awards]], he won three.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.grammy.com/grammys/news/remembering-chris-cornell-sweet-sunshower World|url=https://www.guitarworld.com/guitar-world-readers-vote-soundgardens-chris-cornell-greatest-rock-singer-all-time|date=November 1, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131105034327/http://www.guitarworld.com/guitar-world-readers-vote-soundgardens-chris-cornell-greatest-rock-singer-all-time|archive-date=November 5, 2013}}</ref> In 2025, Cornell was posthumously inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] as a member of Soundgarden.<ref>{{cite web |title=Soundgarden |url=https://rockhall.com/inductees/soundgarden/ |website=Rock & Roll Hall of Fame |access-date=April 28, 2025}}</ref>

==Early life==
Cornell was born Christopher John Boyle on July 20, 1964,<ref name="TheGuardian2017">{{cite web|title=Chris Cornell obituary|url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2017/may/18/chris-cornell-obituary|website=The Guardian|access-date=July 29, 2017|date=May 18, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170729222623/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2017/may/18/chris-cornell-obituary|archive-date=July 29, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/entertainment-arts-39960066 |title=Chris Cornell: Soundgarden star hanged himself |access-date=July 19, 2018 |work=BBC News |date=May 18, 2017}}</ref> in [[Seattle|Seattle, Washington]], where he was raised. His parents are Edward F. Boyle,<ref name="parents">{{cite web|title=King County Marriage Records, 1855-Present – Edward F Boyle – Karen R Cornell|url=https://www.digitalarchives.wa.gov/Record/View/8937AA897DF317577EA17EAE93CE488F|publisher=Washington State Archives – Digital Archives|access-date=May 31, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180423104301/https://www.digitalarchives.wa.gov/Record/View/8937AA897DF317577EA17EAE93CE488F|archive-date=April 23, 2018}}</ref> a pharmacist of [[Irish Catholic]] descent,<ref name="Daily Freeman">{{cite news |url=http://www.dailyfreeman.com/arts-and-entertainment/20131107/chris-cornell-to-play-at-upac-in-kingston |title=Chris Cornell to play at UPAC in Kingston |work=The Daily Freeman |author=Paula Ann Mitchell |date=November 7, 2013 |access-date=June 4, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170604051935/http://www.dailyfreeman.com/arts-and-entertainment/20131107/chris-cornell-to-play-at-upac-in-kingston |archive-date=June 4, 2017}}</ref><ref name="bio"/> and Karen Boyle ({{née}} Cornell),<ref name="parents"/><ref name="bio">{{cite web|title=Chris Cornell Biography (1964–2017)|url=http://www.biography.com/people/chris-cornell-278911|publisher=biography.com|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160508085901/http://www.biography.com/people/chris-cornell-278911|archive-date=May 8, 2016|access-date=May 7, 2016}}</ref> an accountant of [[Jewish]] background and self-proclaimed [[psychic]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Chris Cornell on the Howard Stern Show 6-12-07 (1/6)|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mJSj2beqMTk&t=3m18s|work=YouTube| date=August 6, 2009 |url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180423104301/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mJSj2beqMTk&t=3m18s|archive-date=April 23, 2018}}</ref><ref name="Daily Freeman"/><ref name="LATimes">{{cite web|title=Chris Cornell, who helped reignite hard rock in the 1990s with Soundgarden, dies at 52|url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/music/la-et-ms-chris-cornell-death-obituary-20170518-story.html|work=Los Angeles Times|date=May 18, 2017|access-date=June 3, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170602233933/http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/music/la-et-ms-chris-cornell-death-obituary-20170518-story.html|archive-date=June 2, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Medium with a Message|url=http://archive.seattleweekly.com/1999-04-14/music/medium-with-a-message|newspaper=Seattle Weekly|date=October 6, 2006|access-date=June 3, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170603104641/http://archive.seattleweekly.com/1999-04-14/music/medium-with-a-message|archive-date=June 3, 2017}}</ref> Cornell was one of six children; he had two older brothers and three younger sisters.<ref name="TheGuardian2017"/> He and his siblings adopted his mother's maiden name, Cornell, following their parents' divorce when they were teenagers.<ref name="LATimes"/><ref name="TheGuardian2017" /> Cornell attended Christ the King, a Catholic elementary school,<ref name="Scaggs">{{cite magazine|title=Q&A: Chris Cornell|last=Scaggs|first=Austin|author-link=Austin Scaggs|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|url=http://www.ultimate-guitar.com/news/interviews/chris_cornell_interview.html|date=July 14, 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100818214015/http://www.ultimate-guitar.com/news/interviews/chris_cornell_interview.html|archive-date=August 18, 2010}}</ref> where he performed for the first time in front of a crowd, singing the 1960s anti-war song "[[One Tin Soldier]]".<ref name="Scaggs"/> When he was in seventh grade, his mother pulled him and his sister out of Catholic school for fear they were about to be expelled for being too inquisitive.<ref name="Request">{{cite news|url=http://web.stargate.net/soundgarden/articles/request_10-94.shtml|title=Interview with Request magazine, October 1994|publisher=Request|access-date=June 4, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170530073630/http://web.stargate.net/soundgarden/articles/request_10-94.shtml|archive-date=May 30, 2017}}</ref> He recalled the episode in a 1994 interview with ''Request'' magazine: "With a religion like that, it's not designed for anyone to question. Being young people who have a natural curiosity and half a brain, you're going to start finding inconsistencies, which there are tons of in organized religion. We both sort of made it clear in classroom situations that we didn't get it. 'Explain this to me.' And they couldn't, so we started creating a lot of problems."<ref name="Request"/> Cornell subsequently attended [[Shorewood High School (Washington)|Shorewood High School]], where he later dropped out.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.mtv.com/news/otgr5n/chris-cornell | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221130193814/https://www.mtv.com/news/otgr5n/chris-cornell | url-status=dead | archive-date=November 30, 2022 | title=Chris Cornell | website=[[MTV]] }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://shorewoodhighschool.org/seattle-wa/class-of-1982.html|title=Shorewood HS (SHS) Class of 1982 Alumni List|publisher=Shorewood High School|access-date=June 1, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170729230000/http://shorewoodhighschool.org/seattle-wa/class-of-1982.html|archive-date=July 29, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://patch.com/washington/shoreline/living-in-harmony-shorewoods-chris-cornell|title=Living in Harmony: Shorewood's Chris Cornell|author=Devin Blake|publisher=Patch Network|date=March 6, 2011|access-date=June 1, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170601035401/https://patch.com/washington/shoreline/living-in-harmony-shorewoods-chris-cornell|archive-date=June 1, 2017}}</ref>

[[File:The Shemps (1983).jpg|thumb|left|Cornell (left) with The Shemps in 1983]]
Cornell took piano and guitar lessons as a child.<ref name="Rolling Stone 1994" /> He traced his musical influences back to [[Little Richard]] via [[The Beatles]].<ref name="npr">{{cite web|title=Grunge Pioneer Chris Cornell Tries Neo Soul|url=https://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=101602261|publisher=NPR|date=March 8, 2009|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180410134728/https://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=101602261|archive-date=April 10, 2018}}</ref> He spent a two-year period between the ages of nine and eleven listening to The Beatles after finding a large collection of Beatles records abandoned in the basement of a neighbor's house.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/music/la-et-ms-soundgarden-chris-cornell-badmotorfinger-20170518-story.html |title=From the archives: Read a 1991 Times interview with Chris Cornell on the making of Soundgarden's 'Badmotorfinger' |newspaper=LA Times |access-date=May 19, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170519021720/http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/music/la-et-ms-soundgarden-chris-cornell-badmotorfinger-20170518-story.html |archive-date=May 19, 2017|date=May 18, 2017}}</ref> Cornell described himself at this age as a [[loner]]; he was able to deal with his anxiety around other people through rock music.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chris Cornell: Biography|author=Prato, Greg|url={{AllMusic|class=artist|id=p66582|pure_url=yes}}|website=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=September 3, 2009}}</ref> During his teenage years, he experienced [[severe depression]], dropped out of school, and almost never left the house during a two-year span.<ref name="Guardian">{{cite news |author=Dave Simpson |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2009/mar/13/chris-cornell-interview-soundgarden-audioslave |title=Dave Simpson meets Chris Cornell {{pipe}} Music |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=March 12, 2009 |access-date=July 20, 2016}}</ref> At the age of 12, Cornell had access to [[Alcoholic beverage|alcohol]] and [[cannabis|marijuana]]; he used them daily by 13, stopped for a year, but relapsed at age 15 for another year until he turned to music.<ref name="Rolling Stone 1994"/><ref name="People"/> At 14, he had a bad [[Phencyclidine|PCP]] experience and later had [[panic disorder]] and [[agoraphobia]].<ref name=spin>{{cite web |url=http://www.spin.com/2017/05/chris-cornell-audioslave-interview/ |title=Chris Cornell's 2006 Interview on Audioslave, Addiction, and Reinventing Rock |website=Spin |date=May 17, 2017 |access-date=May 31, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170527120954/http://www.spin.com/2017/05/chris-cornell-audioslave-interview/ |archive-date=May 27, 2017}}</ref>

Cornell credited his mother for saving his life when she bought him a [[snare drum]], the instrument he first adopted on his path to becoming a rock musician.<ref name="LATimes"/> Before he was a successful musician, Cornell worked as a [[busboy]],<ref name="Rolling Stone Australia"/> as a dishwasher,<ref name="Rolling Stone Australia"/> as a [[fish monger]] at a seafood wholesaler,<ref name="Guardian"/> and as a [[Chef#Sous-chef|sous-chef]] at [[Ray's Boathouse]] in Seattle.<ref name="stout">{{cite news|title=As a Paris restaurateur and family man, life is now good for Audioslave rocker|author=Gene Stout|url=http://www.seattlepi.com/pop/267486_cornell21.html|newspaper=Seattle Post-Intelligencer|access-date=February 21, 2008|date=April 20, 2006}}</ref>

In the early 1980s, Cornell was a member of a Seattle-based [[cover band]] called The Shemps, which featured bassist [[Hiro Yamamoto]].<ref name=history>{{cite book|last=Anderson|first=Kyle|title=Accidental Revolution|publisher=St. Martin's Griffin|location=New York|year=2007|isbn=978-0-312-35819-8|pages=[https://archive.org/details/accidentalrevolu0000ande/page/112 112–116]|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/accidentalrevolu0000ande/page/112}}</ref> After Yamamoto left The Shemps, the band recruited guitarist [[Kim Thayil]].<ref name="history"/> Cornell and Yamamoto stayed in contact, and after The Shemps broke up, the pair started [[jam session|jamming]] together, eventually bringing Thayil in to join them.<ref name="history"/>

==Recording career==
===1984–1997 and 2010–2017: Soundgarden===
{{Main|Soundgarden}}
Soundgarden was formed in 1984 by Cornell, Thayil, and Yamamoto, with Cornell originally on drums and vocals. In 1985, they enlisted Scott Sundquist to take over as drummer so that Cornell could concentrate on vocals.<ref>George-Warren, Holly, Patricia Romanowski, and Jon Pareles. ''The Rolling Stone Encyclopedia of Rock & Roll''. Rolling Stone Press. 2001. {{ISBN|978-0-671-43457-1}}.</ref> Soundgarden's first recordings were three songs that appeared on a compilation for [[C/Z Records]] called ''[[Deep Six (album)|Deep Six]]''. In 1986, Sundquist, who by that point had a wife and a child, decided to leave the band and spend time with his family.<ref name=history/> He was replaced by [[Matt Cameron]], the drummer for [[Skin Yard]], who became Soundgarden's permanent drummer.<ref name=history/>

Soundgarden signed to [[Sub Pop]], releasing the ''[[Screaming Life]]'' [[Extended play|EP]] in 1987 and the ''[[Fopp (EP)|Fopp]]'' EP in 1988 (a combination of the two was issued as ''[[Screaming Life/Fopp]]'' in 1990). Though the band was being courted by major labels, they signed to independent label [[SST Records]] in 1988 to release their debut album, ''[[Ultramega OK]]'', for which they earned a [[Grammy Award]] nomination for [[Grammy Award for Best Metal Performance|Best Metal Performance]] in 1990.<ref name="grammy">{{cite news|url=https://www.grammy.com/grammys/artists/soundgarden|title=Soundgarden's GRAMMY Awards history|work=Grammy.com|access-date=October 3, 2019}}</ref> The band subsequently signed with [[A&M Records]], becoming the first [[grunge]] band to sign to a major label.<ref name="Guardian"/>

In 1989, Soundgarden released their second effort and their first album for a major label, ''[[Louder Than Love]]''. Following the album's release, Yamamoto left the band to finish his master's degree in physical chemistry at [[Western Washington University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://exclaim.ca/music/article/soundgarden-ups_downs_of_screaming_life|title=Soundgarden – The Ups and Downs of Screaming Life|author=Jason Schneider|work=Exclaim!|date=October 29, 2012|access-date=March 4, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160806182603/http://exclaim.ca/music/article/soundgarden-ups_downs_of_screaming_life|archive-date=August 6, 2016}}</ref> He was replaced by former [[Nirvana (band)|Nirvana]] guitarist [[Jason Everman]]. Everman was fired following the band's tour in support of ''Louder Than Love''. In 1990, they were joined by a new bassist, [[Ben Shepherd]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spin.com/2013/05/soundgarden-bassist-ben-shepherd-nirvana-lead-guitar/|title=Soundgarden Bassist Ben Shepherd Reflects on Almost Joining Nirvana|work=SPIN|date=May 30, 2013|access-date=March 4, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180304173531/https://www.spin.com/2013/05/soundgarden-bassist-ben-shepherd-nirvana-lead-guitar/|archive-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref>

Along with Nirvana, [[Alice in Chains]], and [[Pearl Jam]], Soundgarden quickly became one of the most successful bands from Seattle's emerging grunge scene in the early 1990s. With Shepherd, the new line-up recorded ''[[Badmotorfinger]]'' in 1991. The album brought the band to a new level of commercial success and exposure amid the sudden popularity and attention given to the Seattle music scene. ''Badmotorfinger'' included the singles "[[Jesus Christ Pose]]", "[[Outshined]]" and "[[Rusty Cage]]". The three singles gained considerable airtime on alternative rock radio stations, while the videos for "Outshined" and "Rusty Cage" gained considerable airtime on MTV. The song "Jesus Christ Pose" and its music video was the subject of widespread controversy in 1991, and the video was removed from MTV's playlist. "Rusty Cage" was later covered by [[Johnny Cash]] on his 1996 album, ''[[Unchained (Johnny Cash album)|Unchained]]''. "[[Room a Thousand Years Wide]]" was released (along with the B-side "HIV Baby") as a 7" single through Sub Pop's ''Single of the Month'' club a full year before the release of ''Badmotorfinger'', and later re-recorded for the album. With ''Badmotorfinger'', Soundgarden found their first mainstream success: it was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Metal Performance in 1992<ref name="grammy"/> and was later ranked number 45 in the October 2006 issue of ''[[Guitar World]]'' on the magazine's list of the 100 greatest guitar albums of all time.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://chud.com/forums/showthread.php?t=93854 |title=Guitar World's (Readers Choice) Greatest 100 Guitar Albums Of All Time |access-date=May 26, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070823050531/http://chud.com/forums/showthread.php?t=93854 |archive-date=August 23, 2007 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Soundgarden's fourth studio album, 1994's ''[[Superunknown]]'', proved to be the band's breakthrough album. Upon its release in March 1994, ''Superunknown'' debuted at number one on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]].<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,301554,00.html|title=Changing of the Garden|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|access-date=October 12, 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080830000510/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0%2C%2C301554%2C00.html|archive-date=August 30, 2008}}</ref> The album launched several successful singles, including "[[Spoonman]]" and "[[Black Hole Sun]]", and brought the band international recognition. ''Superunknown'' achieved quintuple platinum status in the United States,<ref name="search">{{cite web|url=http://riaa.com/goldandplatinumdata.php?table=SEARCH|publisher=[[Recording Industry Association of America]]|title=Gold and Platinum Database Search|access-date=February 12, 2007|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070626050454/http://www.riaa.com/goldandplatinumdata.php?table=SEARCH|archive-date=June 26, 2007}}</ref> triple platinum status in Canada,<ref name="cria">{{cite web |url=http://www.cria.ca/cert_db_search.php |title=CRIA Database Search |publisher=[[Music Canada|Canadian Recording Industry Association]] |access-date=April 4, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091226130540/http://www.cria.ca/cert_db_search.php |archive-date=December 26, 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref> and gold status in the United Kingdom,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bpi.co.uk/platinum/platinumright.asp?rq=search_plat&r_id=3244 |title=Superunknown Certified Awards |publisher=[[British Phonographic Industry]] |access-date=February 19, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080220133205/http://www.bpi.co.uk/platinum/platinumRight.asp?rq=search_plat |archive-date=February 20, 2008}}</ref> Sweden,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hitlistan.se/ |title=Superunknown Certified Awards |publisher=[[IFPI|IFPI Den Svenske Hitlista]] |access-date=February 19, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080223114321/http://www.hitlistan.se/ |archive-date=February 23, 2008 |url-status=dead}}</ref> and the Netherlands.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nvpi.nl/nvpi/pagina.asp?pagkey=60461#resultaat |title=Superunknown Certified Awards |publisher=[[NVPI]] |access-date=February 19, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080103054405/http://www.nvpi.nl/nvpi/pagina.asp?pagkey=60461#resultaat |archive-date=January 3, 2008 |url-status=dead}}</ref> ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' gave ''Superunknown'' four out of five stars. Reviewer J.D. Considine said ''Superunknown'' "demonstrates far greater range than many bands manage in an entire career". Considine criticized "Black Hole Sun" and "Half", stating that the former is "not a very good song", while the latter "is the virtual definition of a B-side."<ref>{{cite magazine|author=Consideine, J.D.|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/artists/soundgarden/albums/album/112428/review/5942536/superunknown|title=Soundgarden: ''Superunknown''|magazine=Rolling Stone|access-date=October 12, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080705160513/http://www.rollingstone.com/artists/soundgarden/albums/album/112428/review/5942536/superunknown |archive-date=July 5, 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Jon Pareles]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'' said that "''Superunknown'' actually tries to broaden its audience by breaking [[Heavy metal music|heavy-metal]] genre barriers that Soundgarden used to accept." He added that "Soundgarden ... want[s] something different from standard heavy metal."<ref>{{cite news|author=Pareles, Jon |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1994/03/06/arts/recordings-view-lightening-up-on-the-gloom-in-grunge.html |title=RECORDINGS VIEW; Lightening Up On the Gloom In Grunge |website=[[The New York Times]] |date=March 6, 1994}}</ref> David Browne of ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' gave the album an A, saying "Soundgarden is pumped and primed on ''Superunknown'', and they deliver the goods." He praised it as a "hard-rock milestone—a boiling vat of volcanic power, record-making smarts, and '90s anomie and anxiety that sets a new standard for anything called metal."<ref>{{cite magazine|author=Browne, David|url=https://ew.com/article/1994/03/11/superunknown/|title=Garden Party|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|access-date=October 12, 2008|date=March 11, 1994|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080922153446/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,301370,00.html|archive-date=September 22, 2008}}</ref> The album was nominated for the [[Grammy Award for Best Rock Album]] in 1995.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1995/02/26/arts/pop-view-playing-grammy-roulette.html |title=POP VIEW; Playing Grammy Roulette |work=The New York Times |author=Pareles, Jon |access-date=August 3, 2008 |date=February 26, 1995 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120712191302/http://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=990CE2DD113CF935A15751C0A963958260 |archive-date=July 12, 2012}}</ref> Two singles from ''Superunknown'', "Black Hole Sun" and "Spoonman", won Grammy Awards,<ref name="grammy"/> and the music video for "Black Hole Sun" won a [[MTV Video Music Award]] and a [[Clio Awards|Clio Award]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://archive.seattletimes.com/archive/19950602/2124171/music-notes |title=Music Notes |newspaper=The Seattle Times |author=Macdonald, Patrick |access-date=August 3, 2008 |date=June 2, 1995 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120923133356/http://community.seattletimes.nwsource.com/archive/?date=19950602&slug=2124171 |archive-date=September 23, 2012}}</ref> ''Superunknown'' was ranked number 336 on ''Rolling Stone'' magazine's list of the [[Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time|500 greatest albums of all time]],<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/features/coverstory/featuregen.asp?pid=2164|title=The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time|access-date=May 6, 2008|magazine=Rolling Stone|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080614194909/http://www.rollingstone.com/features/coverstory/featuregen.asp%3Fpid%3D2164 |archive-date=June 14, 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref> and "Black Hole Sun" was ranked number 25 on [[VH1]]'s list of the 100 greatest songs of the '90s.<ref name="greatest90s">{{cite web|url=http://www.vh1.com/shows/dyn/the_greatest/127759/episode_featured_copy.jhtml|publisher=[[VH1]]|title=VH1: 100 Greatest Songs of the '90s|access-date=August 9, 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080724023220/http://www.vh1.com/shows/dyn/the_greatest/127759/episode_featured_copy.jhtml|archive-date=July 24, 2008}}</ref>

The band's fifth album was 1996's self-produced ''[[Down on the Upside]]''. The album spawned several singles, including "[[Pretty Noose]]", "[[Burden in My Hand]]" and "[[Blow Up the Outside World]]". ''Down on the Upside'' was notably less heavy than the group's preceding albums and marked a further departure from the band's grunge roots. Soundgarden explained at the time that it wanted to experiment with other sounds.<ref>{{cite web|author=Turman, Katherine|title=Soundgarden: Seattle's Sonic Boom|url=http://web.stargate.net/soundgarden/articles/hypno_1996.shtml|publisher=Hypno|access-date=October 12, 2008|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080422022936/http://web.stargate.net/soundgarden/articles/hypno_1996.shtml|archive-date=April 22, 2008}}</ref> David Browne of ''Entertainment Weekly'' said, "Few bands since Led Zeppelin have so crisply mixed instruments both acoustic and electric."<ref>{{cite magazine |first=David |last=Browne |url=https://ew.com/article/1996/05/24/down-upside/ |title=Down on the Upside |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |access-date=October 19, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090202082937/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,292725,00.html |archive-date=February 2, 2009 |url-status=live |date=May 24, 1996}}</ref>

However, tensions within the group arose during the sessions, with Thayil and Cornell reportedly clashing over Cornell's desire to shift away from the heavy guitar riffing that had become the band's trademark.<ref>{{cite magazine|author=John Colapinto |author-link= John Colapinto |title=Soundgarden Split|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|access-date=October 19, 2008|url=http://web.stargate.net/soundgarden/articles/rs_5-29-97.shtml|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090310130644/http://web.stargate.net/soundgarden/articles/rs_5-29-97.shtml|archive-date=March 10, 2009}}</ref> Despite favorable reviews, the album couldn't match the sales of ''Superunknown''.<ref name="search"/>

In 1997, Soundgarden received another Grammy award nomination for the lead single "Pretty Noose".<ref name="grammy"/> As tensions grew within the band, reportedly due to internal strife over its creative direction, Soundgarden announced that it was disbanding on April 9, 1997. In a 1998 interview, Thayil said, "It was pretty obvious from everybody's general attitude over the course of the previous half-year that there was some dissatisfaction."<ref>Gilbert, Jeff. "Sound of Silence". ''[[Guitar World]]''. February 1998.</ref>

[[File:Soundgarden Chicago.jpg|thumb|Cornell, Cameron and Shepherd performing with Soundgarden at [[Lollapalooza]] 2010]]

On January 1, 2010, Cornell alluded to a Soundgarden reunion via his Twitter account, writing: "The 12-year break is over and school is back in session. Sign up now. Knights of the Soundtable ride again!" The message linked to a website that featured a picture of the group performing live and a place for fans to enter their e-mail address to get updates on the reunion. Entering that information unlocked an archival video for the song "Get on the Snake" from Soundgarden's second studio album, 1989's ''[[Louder Than Love]]''.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1628964/20100104/soundgarden.jhtml |title=Soundgarden's Chris Cornell announces reunion |last=Kaufman |first=Gil |date=January 4, 2010 |work=MTV News |publisher=MTV Networks |access-date=January 10, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100114021623/http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1628964/20100104/soundgarden.jhtml |archive-date=January 14, 2010}}</ref>

In March 2010, Soundgarden announced that they would be headlining [[Lollapalooza]] 2010. Soundgarden made the announcement through their website and email list.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.soundgardenworld.com/news/2010-03-17/soundgarden |title=Soundgarden |date=March 16, 2010 |website=Soundgarden World |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100409061847/http://www.soundgardenworld.com/news/2010-03-17/soundgarden |archive-date=April 9, 2010 |url-status=dead |access-date=April 25, 2018}}</ref> On April 16, 2010, Soundgarden held a secret show at the [[The Showbox|Showbox Theater]] on First Avenue in downtown Seattle, publicized via the band's mailing list. The show was billed as ''Nudedragons'', an [[anagram]] for Soundgarden.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=138636|title=Reunited Soundgarden to Perform as Nudedragons at Tonight's Concert|publisher=BlabberMouth|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100419165840/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=138636|archive-date=April 19, 2010}}</ref>

Asked in August 2010 if Soundgarden would record new material, Cornell replied, "it would be exciting to record one song, to hear how Soundgarden-ish that might be this much time later. But for me, it's been more of a trip relearning the songs and playing them together. Some of the songs we're approaching we've never played live."<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=144703|title=Soundgarden: After 13 Years, The Grunge Gods Return. Now What?|date=August 17, 2010|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|access-date=August 17, 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100820122658/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=144703|archive-date=August 20, 2010}}</ref>

Soundgarden made their first television appearance since their reunion on the second episode of [[Conan O'Brien]]'s [[TBS (American TV channel)|TBS show]], ''[[Conan (talk show)|Conan]]'', on November 9, 2010, and toured North America in summer 2011.{{citation needed|date=December 2019}} In summer 2012, Soundgarden released a new single and video, "Live to Rise", for ''[[The Avengers (2012 film)|The Avengers]]'' movie soundtrack.<ref name="LTR"/> Their sixth album, ''[[King Animal]]'', was released in November 2012 to largely positive reviews.<ref name="MC">{{cite web|url=https://www.metacritic.com/music/king-animal/soundgarden|title=King Animal – Soundgarden|work=[[Metacritic]]|access-date=October 3, 2019}}</ref>
