===''Shogun'' and departure of Travis Smith (2008–2009)===
{{Listen
 |filename     = Trivium - Kirisute Gomen.ogg
 |title        = "Kirisute Gomen"
 |description  = The first song from ''[[Shogun (Trivium album)|Shogun]]'' (2008)
}}
Trivium started working on a new album with producer [[Nick Raskulinecz]] in October 2007.<ref>{{cite news
| title = Metal Injection gets exclusive details on upcoming Trivium album
| work = Metal Injection
| url = http://metalinjection.net/latest-news/metal-injection-gets-exclusive-details-on-upcoming-trivium-album
| date = January 30, 2008
| access-date = March 19, 2008
| archive-date = June 5, 2008
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080605035456/http://metalinjection.net/latest-news/metal-injection-gets-exclusive-details-on-upcoming-trivium-album
| url-status = live
}}</ref> Heafy stated he wanted to bring back the screaming that was found on ''Ascendancy'', and the band said they chose not to work with Suecof again because they already recorded three albums with him and wanted to explore new ideas.<ref>{{cite journal
|date=February 2008
|author=Wiederhorn, Jon
|title=Brutal 2008 Preview&nbsp;– Trivium
|journal=[[Revolver Magazine]]}}</ref> Recording ended June 2008.<ref>{{cite web
| title = Trivium End Recording and begin post-production
| publisher = Triviumworld
| url = http://www.triviumworld.com/news/news.php?uid=128
| date = June 20, 2008
| access-date = June 20, 2008
| archive-date = August 1, 2008
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080801064601/http://www.triviumworld.com/news/news.php?uid=128
| url-status = live
}}</ref>
In an interview with the UK's ''[[Metal Hammer]]'' magazine in May 2008, Heafy said that their new album was to have "more thrash influences, more screaming."<ref>{{cite journal|date=May 2008 |author=Head, Richard |title=Trivium Discuss Upcoming Album |journal=[[Metal Hammer]]}}</ref> He told [[Revolver (magazine)|Revolver]] magazine, "For the first time, we can't look at our songs and say who the riffs sound like. We're really making our own stuff and our own kind of music and art form, and that's exciting."<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/BlabberMouth.Net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=97896|title=Trivium: Japanese, Australian Dates Announced|date=May 28, 2008|work=Blabbermouth.net|publisher=Roadrunner Records|access-date=March 8, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080602231027/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=97896|archive-date=June 2, 2008|df=mdy-all}}</ref> In September 2008, Trivium released their fourth full-length album, ''[[Shogun (Trivium album)|Shogun]]''. The album sold 24,000 copies in the United States in its first week of release, debuting at number 23 on the [[Billboard 200]] chart as well as number 1 in the UK Rock Album Charts.<ref name="sales">{{cite news|url=http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=106423|title=Trivium: Shogun First-Week Sales Revealed|date=October 8, 2008|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|access-date=October 8, 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081013161624/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=106423|archive-date=October 13, 2008|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

Trivium toured extensively throughout 2009 in support of ''[[Shogun (Trivium album)|Shogun]]'', with two headline legs of the US, a headline slot on the [[Mayhem Festival]] second stage, an Australia/Japan leg,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/trivium-guitarist-on-touring-and-shogun/|title=TRIVIUM Guitarist On Touring And 'Shogun'|last=Blabbermouth|date=April 26, 2009|website=BLABBERMOUTH.NET|access-date=January 25, 2018|archive-date=January 26, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180126070806/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/trivium-guitarist-on-touring-and-shogun/|url-status=live}}</ref> as well as a conclusive UK run in March 2010. Throughout their headline runs, they were supported by [[Chimaira]], [[Darkest Hour (band)|Darkest Hour]], [[Dirge Within]], [[Whitechapel (band)|Whitechapel]], [[Rise to Remain]] and [[Black Tide]]. They were also booked as a co-headliner for Australia's [[Soundwave (Australian music festival)|Soundwave Festival]] in February 2010.

Travis Smith unofficially left the band on the second leg of the "Into the Mouth of Hell We Tour" tour. On February 4, 2010, the band announced that Travis had indeed officially left the band and fill-in drummer, ex-drum tech, Nick Augusto, was replacing him. Augusto is a former member of Maruta and Metal Militia, in which he played with Gregoletto.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.trivium.org/board_posts/trivium-announce-nick-augusto-as-new-drummer |title=Trivium Announce Nick Augusto As New Drummer |website=Trivium.org |date=February 4, 2010 |access-date=April 10, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100208101319/http://www.trivium.org/board_posts/trivium-announce-nick-augusto-as-new-drummer |archive-date=February 8, 2010 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> While Trivium's relationship with Smith had deteriorated over the years, the band had no immediate plans to replace him when he announced in late October 2009 that he would be sitting out the tour to take care of "some personal business." However, Augusto's skill while filling in for the tour convinced the band that he could improve their creativity and live performances.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wiederhorn |first=Jon|date=2010-02-16 |title=Trivium Frontman Explains Firing of Drummer Travis Smith |url=https://noisecreep.com/trivium-frontman-explains-firing-of-drummer-travis-smith/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180529080916/https://noisecreep.com/trivium-frontman-explains-firing-of-drummer-travis-smith/ |archive-date=May 29, 2018 |access-date=2025-03-25 |website=Noisecreep |language=en}}</ref>

Trivium contributed to the ''[[God of War III]]'' soundtrack by recording the song, "Shattering the Skies Above". It is exclusively included on ''[[God of War: Blood & Metal]]'', a [[music download|digital]] EP that comes with the ''Ultimate Edition'' of the game and is available from the [[iTunes Store]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=130855 |title=BLABBERMOUTH.NET - TRIVIUM: New Songtitle Revealed |website=Roadrunnerrecords.com |access-date=April 10, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100105103808/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=130855 |archive-date=January 5, 2010 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> The band has also recorded a cover of the song "[[Slave New World]]" by [[Sepultura]]. "Shattering the Skies Above" was also released exclusively to their fanclub (TriviumWorld) on February 12, 2010 and was released widely on February 15.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.trivium.org/ |title=Trivium Official Website: Vengeance Falls Music, Videos, Photos, Tour Dates |website=Trivium.org |access-date=2014-03-04 |archive-date=April 25, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110425114318/http://www.trivium.org/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The next day their Sepultura cover "Slave New World" was released as a free download for members of the UK via Metal Hammer UK. Both of aforementioned songs re-issued on their deluxe version of the album "In Waves".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.metalhammer.co.uk/news/trivium-slave-new-world-sepultura-cover-world-exclusive|title=Trivium 'Slave New World' Sepultura Cover – World Exclusive|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100215220853/http://www.metalhammer.co.uk/news/trivium-slave-new-world-sepultura-cover-world-exclusive|archive-date=February 15, 2010|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

===''In Waves'' (2010–2012)===
In an interview with ''Guitar World'', it was stated that for their next studio album, Trivium would "forgo the complex epic compositions, tricked-out leads and seven-string guitars that characterized its past two albums" and instead take an approach similar to that of ''Ascendancy'' by using uncluttered riffs, Drop C# tuning, and more straightforward solos. Heafy stated "When we did ''Ascendancy'', we were writing specifically for the songs, not to show how well we could play. That wasn't exactly the case with our next two records."<ref name="guitarworld.com">{{cite web |url=http://www.guitarworld.com/article/trivium039s_pursuit |title=Trivium: In the Studio – Guitar World |website=Guitarworld.com |date=January 18, 2011 |access-date=October 26, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110511210355/http://www.guitarworld.com/article/trivium039s_pursuit |archive-date=May 11, 2011 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> In the bonus content for the November 2011 issue of ''Guitar World'', Heafy said the lower tuning was to make his vocals easier due to the number of concerts the band plays.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.guitarworld.com/trivium-waves-video-lessons?page=0,1|title=Trivium: 'In Waves' Video Lessons|website=GuitarWorld.com|date=September 21, 2011|access-date=January 11, 2012|archive-date=October 3, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111003195723/http://www.guitarworld.com/trivium-waves-video-lessons?page=0,1|url-status=live}} {{Dead link|date=March 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4zTJ7s2sr6o |title=Trivium: 'In Waves' Video Lesson - "Inception of the End" |date=2011-09-26 |last=Guitar World |access-date= |via=YouTube}} [https://web.archive.org/web/20240322064037/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4zTJ7s2sr6o Archived] from the original on March 22, 2024. Retrieved March 30, 2025</ref>

On June 6, ''[[Metal Hammer]]'' revealed that the album would be titled ''[[In Waves (Trivium album)|In Waves]]'' and that it would be released on August 9, 2011.<ref name="metalhammer.co.uk">{{cite magazine |url=http://www.metalhammer.co.uk/news/trivium-name-new-album-2/ |title=Blog Archive » Trivium Name New Album |magazine=[[Metal Hammer]] |date=June 6, 2011 |access-date=July 9, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130722092309/http://www.metalhammer.co.uk/news/trivium-name-new-album-2/ |archive-date=July 22, 2013 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> On June 19, Trivium debuted two new songs live in Birmingham entitled "Dusk Dismantled" and "Black". On the June 28, "Dusk Dismantled" was released to TriviumWorld users only; it was released to general public on the 29th. On July 13, the premiere of "Inception of the End" was released to the general public on the website [[Hot Topic]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://community.hottopic.com/content/world-premiere-hear-triviums-new-track-inception-end |title=World Premiere! Hear Trivium's New Track "Inception Of The End" &#124; Hot Topic |website=Community.hottopic.com |access-date=October 26, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111003225026/http://community.hottopic.com/content/world-premiere-hear-triviums-new-track-inception-end |archive-date=October 3, 2011 |df=mdy-all }}</ref>

''In Waves'' was released in August 2011 worldwide and received generally positive reviews. Kerrang! described the album as "draws from the band's entire repertoire and shapes what it finds into a defining and definitive set". A special edition was released featuring bonus tracks "Ensnare the Sun", "A Grey So Dark", "Drowning in Slow Motion", the "Slave New World" cover, and the single from the God of War III soundtrack "Shattering the Skies Above".

Trivium participated in a co-headlining trek with Swedish melodic death metal band [[In Flames]] in both Europe and North America. European support came from [[Ghost (Swedish band)|Ghost]], [[Rise to Remain]] and Insense. North American support came from [[Veil of Maya]] and Kyng. Additionally, Miss May I and The Ghost Inside joined Trivium during the [[In Waves (Trivium album)|In Waves]] 2011 European tour. They also performed at the [[Metaltown Festival]] and [[Download Festival]] in June 2012. From July 13 to August 28, 2012, Trivium took part in [[Metal Hammer]]'s "[[Trespass America Festival]]" headlined by [[Five Finger Death Punch]] with additional support from [[Battlecross]], [[God Forbid]], [[Pop Evil]], [[Emmure]] and [[Killswitch Engage]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Long|last=Paul|date=April 24, 2012|url=http://knac.com/article.asp?ArticleID=8692|title=Trespass America Touring Fest Breaks Out: FFDP, Killswitch, Trivium, God Forbid, Hit the Road|work=KNAC|access-date=May 31, 2012|archive-date=October 20, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121020223732/http://knac.com/article.asp?ArticleID=8692|url-status=live}}</ref> On October 15, 2012, Trivium commenced a European headlining tour, supported by [[Caliban (band)|Caliban]], [[As I Lay Dying (band)|As I Lay Dying]] and [[Upon A Burning Body]].

===''Vengeance Falls'' and departure of Nick Augusto (2013–2015)===
[[File:20140614-080-Nova Rock 2014-Trivium-Trivium.JPG|thumb|270px|Trivium performing at [[Nova Rock Festival]] in 2014]]

The band toured for ''In Waves'' until the end of the year. Heafy stated that they would start recording a new album in February 2013 and they already have around 13 demos made.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.metalinsider.net/interviews/matt-heafy-discusses-new-side-project-mrityu-and-recording-plans-for-triviums-new-album|title=Matt Heafy Discusses New Side Project Mrityu And Recording Plans For Trivium's New Album|work=Metal Insider|date=August 20, 2012|access-date=September 22, 2015|archive-date=August 22, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120822204317/http://www.metalinsider.net/interviews/matt-heafy-discusses-new-side-project-mrityu-and-recording-plans-for-triviums-new-album|url-status=live}}</ref>

On January 14, 2013, Heafy announced via Twitter that the band had entered the studio. It was later revealed that they hired [[David Draiman]] of the heavy metal bands [[Device (heavy metal band)|Device]] and [[Disturbed (band)|Disturbed]] as a producer. In an interview, David Draiman revealed to Thrash Hits that the title of Trivium's forthcoming sixth album was ''[[Vengeance Falls]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thrashhits.com/2013/05/sxsw-2013-the-day-raz-went-to-david-draimans-house/|title=SXSW 2013: The day Raz went to David Draiman's house|publisher=Thrash Hits|date=2013-05-28|access-date=2014-03-04|archive-date=June 8, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130608054109/http://www.thrashhits.com/2013/05/sxsw-2013-the-day-raz-went-to-david-draimans-house/|url-status=live}}</ref>

''Vengeance Falls'' was produced at a studio in Austin, Texas and was mixed by [[Colin Richardson]], who has previously worked with [[Fear Factory]], [[Cannibal Corpse]], [[Machine Head (band)|Machine Head]], [[Napalm Death]], [[Slipknot (band)|Slipknot]] and [[Bullet for My Valentine]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=190455 |title=Vengeance Falls production and mix|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=May 27, 2013}}</ref>

On July 23, 2013, Trivium announced a United States headlining tour, co-headlining with [[DevilDriver]], with supporting acts [[After the Burial]] and [[Sylosis]], which would reveal the first information of the new album.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://loudwire.com/trivium-devildriver-2013-north-american-tour-after-the-burial-sylosis/ |title=Trivium and DevilDriver Announce 2013 North American Tour with After the Burial + Sylosis |website=Loudwire.com |date=2013-07-23 |access-date=2014-03-04 |archive-date=July 25, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130725050818/http://loudwire.com/trivium-devildriver-2013-north-american-tour-after-the-burial-sylosis/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Vengeance Falls'' was released on October 15, 2013.<ref name="roadrunnerrecords.com">{{cite web |last=Freeman |first=Phil |url=http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/news/trivium-vf-20130731 |title=Trivium - "Vengeance Falls" On October 15! |publisher=Roadrunner Records |date=2013-07-30 |access-date=2014-03-04 |archive-date=August 7, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130807043230/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/news/trivium-vf-20130731 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On July 31, 2013, the new song "Brave This Storm" was released for streaming and made available to download for free.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.trivium.fm/ |title=Trivium / Brave This Storm |website=Trivium.fm |access-date=2014-03-04 |archive-date=July 23, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130723203149/http://www.trivium.fm/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> On August 23, 2013, it was announced that Trivium would be playing at Australia's Soundwave Festival in late February and early March 2014.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://soundwavefestival.com/lineup/trivium |title=Soundwave Festival 2014 |website=Soundwavefestival.com |access-date=2014-03-04 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140305075608/http://soundwavefestival.com/lineup/trivium |archive-date=March 5, 2014 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> Trivium recorded a music video for the single "Strife" with director Ramon Boutviseth ([[All That Remains (band)|All That Remains]], [[For Today (band)|For Today]], [[Fear Factory]])<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.theprp.com/2013/07/20/news/trivium-filming-new-music-video/ |title=Trivium Filming New Music Video &#124; Theprp.com – Metal, Hardcore And Rock News, Reviews And More |website=Theprp.com |date=July 20, 2013 |access-date=2014-03-04 |archive-date=July 24, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130724015215/http://www.theprp.com/2013/07/20/news/trivium-filming-new-music-video/ |url-status=live }}</ref> which was made available for free download to anyone who pre-ordered ''Vengeance Falls''.<ref name="roadrunnerrecords.com"/>

On October 8, 2013, the album was made available for streaming on the band's website.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/photo.php?fbid=10151728773416896&set=a.56786161895.71500.6816136895&type=1&relevant_count=1  |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/facebook/6816136895/10151728773416896 |archive-date=2022-02-26 |url-access=limited|title=Trivium - Tijdlijnfoto's |publisher=[[Facebook]] |access-date=2014-03-04}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

On May 7, 2014, it was announced that drummer Nick Augusto had departed from the band. He was replaced by [[Mat Madiro]], who had been the band's drum technician.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/trivium-parts-ways-with-drummer-nick-augusto/ |title=TRIVIUM Parts Ways With Drummer NICK AUGUSTO |work=[[Blabbermouth.net]] |access-date=2014-05-07 |archive-date=May 8, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140508025623/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/trivium-parts-ways-with-drummer-nick-augusto/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===''Silence in the Snow'' and departure of Mat Madiro (2015–2016)===
In fall of 2014, Beaulieu announced that the band would be working on the follow-up of ''Vengeance Falls'' in 2015, and that he hoped that the album would be released in Fall of the same year.<ref>{{cite web|title=Trivium Hoping to Release New Album Next Fall|url=http://www.ultimate-guitar.com/news/upcoming_releases/trivium_hoping_to_release_new_album_next_fall.html|access-date=January 1, 2015|archive-date=October 10, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141010220810/http://www.ultimate-guitar.com/news/upcoming_releases/trivium_hoping_to_release_new_album_next_fall.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On July 17, 2015, the band launched a website "snow.trivium.org" teasing the new album. They also changed their Facebook profile to the same picture as on the website, hinting at the release of the new album.<ref name="trivium1">{{cite web |url=http://snow.trivium.org/ |title=Trivium |website=Snow.trivium.org |access-date=2015-07-31 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150802001504/http://snow.trivium.org/ |archive-date=August 2, 2015 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> On July 24, the band posted a six-day countdown on their website.<ref name="trivium1" /> An unofficial picture surfaced online on July 29, suggesting the new album title to be ''[[Silence in the Snow]]'' and revealing three new featured songs: "Silence in the Snow", "Dead and Gone" and "Until the World Goes Cold". This picture also suggested a release date of October 2, 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://i.imgur.com/DMNMmZo.jpg |format=JPG |title=Photographic image |website=I.imgur.com |access-date=2015-07-31 |archive-date=November 7, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151107033654/http://i.imgur.com/DMNMmZo.jpg |url-status=live }}</ref> This information was confirmed on July 30 when the band premiered the music video for the title track once the countdown ended.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/trivium-returns-with-silence-in-the-snow-album-video/| title=TRIVIUM Returns With 'Silence In The Snow' Album, Video| work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]| date=30 July 2015| access-date=30 July 2015| archive-date=August 1, 2015| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150801185945/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/trivium-returns-with-silence-in-the-snow-album-video/| url-status=live}}</ref> On July 31, 2015, the band revealed the track list and the album artwork, and ''[[Silence in the Snow]]'' was made available for pre-order.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://music.apple.com/gb/album/silence-in-snow-special-edition/1022897923 |title=iTunes - Music - Silence In the Snow (Special Edition) by Trivium |website=[[iTunes]] |access-date=2015-09-06 |archive-date=November 7, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151107033655/https://itunes.apple.com/gb/album/silence-in-snow-special-edition/id1022897923 |url-status=live }}</ref> On August 7, the band premiered two new songs, "Silence in the Snow" and "Blind Leading the Blind" during their performance at [[Bloodstock Open Air]]. On August 27, Trivium premiered the music video for their third single "Until the World Goes Cold",<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/Trivium/posts/10153188964166896  |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/facebook/6816136895/10153188964166896 |archive-date=2022-02-26 |url-access=limited|title=Trivium - Watch the video premiere of 'Until The World... |publisher=[[Facebook]] |access-date=2015-09-06}}{{cbignore}}</ref> and the album was released on October 2.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/trivium-track-by-track-breakdown-of-silence-in-the-snow-video/|title=TRIVIUM: Track-By-Track Breakdown Of 'Silence In The Snow' (Video)|last=Blabbermouth|date=October 7, 2015|website=BLABBERMOUTH.NET|access-date=December 26, 2018|archive-date=October 8, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151008211600/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/trivium-track-by-track-breakdown-of-silence-in-the-snow-video/|url-status=live}}</ref>

On December 2, Trivium re-released ''Ember to Inferno'', titling it ''[[Ember to Inferno|Ember to Inferno: Ab Initio]]''. The deluxe version of the release contained two discs. The second disk included 13 bonus tracks which consisted of the early demos ''Ruber'' (the "Red Demo"), ''Caeruleus'' (the "Blue Demo") and ''Flavus'' (the "Yellow Demo").<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/trivium-to-re-release-hard-to-find-debut-ember-to-inferno/|title=TRIVIUM To Re-Release Hard-To-Find Debut 'Ember To Inferno'|last=Blabbermouth|date=October 14, 2016|website=BLABBERMOUTH.NET|access-date=December 26, 2018|archive-date=October 17, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161017192350/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/trivium-to-re-release-hard-to-find-debut-ember-to-inferno/|url-status=live}}</ref>

On December 5, the band performed at [[Knotfest]] Mexico, where it was revealed that drummer Mat Madiro had been replaced by Paul Wandtke. The band didn't make an official announcement until three days later, on their Facebook page.<ref>{{cite web|title=Trivium Recruits Drummer Paul Wandtke|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/trivium-recruits-drummer-paul-wandtke/|website=Blabbermouth.net|date=December 5, 2015|access-date=December 5, 2015|archive-date=December 6, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151206230219/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/trivium-recruits-drummer-paul-wandtke/|url-status=live}}</ref> Paul Wandtke joined the band after Heafy asked [[Dream Theater]]'s [[John Petrucci]] for suggestions; Petrucci then asked [[Mike Mangini]], who recommended Wandtke.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.moderndrummer.com/2016/01/on-the-beat-with-paul-wandtke-of-trivium-working-on-the-same-wavelength/|title=On the Beat With Paul Wandtke of Trivium: Working on the Same Wavelength|website=Moderndrummer.com|date=January 11, 2016|access-date=February 21, 2017|archive-date=October 21, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171021221026/http://www.moderndrummer.com/2016/01/on-the-beat-with-paul-wandtke-of-trivium-working-on-the-same-wavelength/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/new-trivium-drummer-was-recommended-by-dream-theaters-mike-mangini/|title=New TRIVIUM Drummer Was Recommended By DREAM THEATER's MIKE MANGINI|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=December 8, 2015|access-date=February 21, 2017|archive-date=December 10, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151210082049/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/new-trivium-drummer-was-recommended-by-dream-theaters-mike-mangini/|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Arrival of Alex Bent and ''The Sin and the Sentence'' (2016–2019) ===
[[file:Trivium - Novarock - 2016-06-10-14-02-46.jpg|thumb|270px|Trivium at [[Nova Rock]] 2016]]
On October 14, 2016, Trivium headlined at the Rock And Shock festival at The Palladium in Worcester, Massachusetts.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.setlist.fm/setlist/trivium/2016/the-palladium-worcester-ma-43fd6b33.html|title=Trivium Setlist|date=October 14, 2016|work=[[Setlist.fm]]|access-date=August 1, 2020|archive-date=September 2, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230902224416/https://www.setlist.fm/setlist/trivium/2016/the-palladium-worcester-ma-43fd6b33.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In late 2016, Beaulieu stated that the band would spend most of 2017 working on their new album.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/next-trivium-album-will-definitely-be-released-in-2017/|title=Next TRIVIUM Album Will 'Definitely' Be Released In 2017|date=October 8, 2016|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|access-date=January 12, 2017|archive-date=October 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161009150506/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/next-trivium-album-will-definitely-be-released-in-2017/|url-status=live}}</ref> In an interview, Gregoletto stated that new material will be more 'extreme' and that the band will return to featuring screaming vocals on the new album.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://distortedsoundmag.com/interview-paolo-gregoletto-trivium/|title=INTERVIEW: Paolo Gregoletto - Trivium - Distorted Sound Magazine|date=February 22, 2017|website=Distortedsoundmag.com|access-date=October 21, 2017|archive-date=February 23, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170223182345/http://distortedsoundmag.com/interview-paolo-gregoletto-trivium/|url-status=live}}</ref> The band was announced as one of the acts on the 2017 edition of [[Wacken Open Air]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wacken.com/de/bands/bands-billing/detail/trivium-2017/|title=Wacken Open Air - Detail|website=Wacken.com|access-date=January 12, 2017|archive-date=April 9, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170409234838/http://www.wacken.com/de/bands/bands-billing/detail/trivium-2017/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In early 2017, the band parted ways with Wandtke. The replacement [[Alex Bent]], formerly of [[Battlecross]], was announced on January 23.<ref name="AlexBentMetalSucks"/>

On July 26, 2017, the band began teasing on their web page with the message "VIII. I.", indicating the date "August 1".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.metalinjection.net/upcoming-releases/trivium-begin-teasing-new-album|title=TRIVIUM Begin Teasing New Album|website=Wall Of Sound|first=Robert|last=Pasbani|date=2017-07-26|access-date=2017-08-02|archive-date=July 29, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170729135117/http://www.metalinjection.net/upcoming-releases/trivium-begin-teasing-new-album|url-status=live}}</ref> On August 1, 2017, the band released the new single "The Sin and the Sentence", accompanied with a music video for their forthcoming new album, which aimed to be released later that year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://teamrock.com/news/2017-08-01/watch-trivium-in-the-sin-and-the-sentence-video|title=Watch Trivium in The Sin And The Sentence video|website=[[Teamrock.com]]|first=Scott|last=Munro|date=2017-08-01|access-date=2017-08-02|archive-date=August 1, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170801194542/http://teamrock.com/news/2017-08-01/watch-trivium-in-the-sin-and-the-sentence-video|url-status=live}}</ref> To promote the album, the band announced a co-headlining North American tour with [[Arch Enemy]]  in fall 2017 with [[While She Sleeps]] and [[Fit for an Autopsy]] as support acts.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/trivium-and-arch-enemy-to-join-forces-for-north-american-tour-blabbermouth-net-presale-available/|title=TRIVIUM And ARCH ENEMY To Join Forces For North American Tour; BLABBERMOUTH.NET Presale Available|website=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=2017-08-02|access-date=2017-08-02|archive-date=August 2, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170802212343/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/trivium-and-arch-enemy-to-join-forces-for-north-american-tour-blabbermouth-net-presale-available/|url-status=live}}</ref> On August 24, the band released the second single "The Heart From Your Hate" and revealed the track listing and release date of their new album. ''[[The Sin and the Sentence]]'' released on October 20, 2017, and was received positively by both fans and critics alike.{{Citation needed|date=January 2019}}

On October 25, 2018, just over a year after the album's release, Heafy announced that he had to fly home to Orlando to be with his wife for the birth of their children, and as a result, would be sitting out the remainder of Trivium's ongoing North American tour with [[Light the Torch]] and [[Avatar (band)|Avatar]]. He announced that the band would be working with Light the Torch and ex-[[Killswitch Engage]] frontman [[Howard Jones (American musician)|Howard Jones]] and Avatar frontman Johannes Eckerström, as well as [[YouTube]] personality and musician [[Jared Dines]] to continue the tour without him. Dines would take over Heafy's guitar parts, while Beaulieu, Gregoletto, Jones and Eckerström would handle vocals.{{Citation needed|date=January 2019}}

The band received a Grammy nomination for the song "Betrayer" at the [[61st Annual Grammy Awards]] in 2019 for the [[Grammy Award for Best Metal Performance|Best Metal Performance]], but lost to [[High on Fire]]'s "Electric Messiah".{{Citation needed|date=March 2025}}

=== ''What the Dead Men Say'' and ''In the Court of the Dragon'' (2020–2023) ===
Trivium was announced as an opening act for [[Megadeth]] and [[Lamb of God (band)|Lamb of God]] on their summer 2020 tour called "The Metal Tour of the Year", which was rescheduled for the summer of 2021 due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. [[In Flames]] was originally slated as an additional opening act, but were forced to withdraw from the tour due to international visa issues caused by the pandemic, and were later replaced by [[Hatebreed]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/megadeth-lamb-of-god-announce-2020-north-american-tour-trivium-and-in-flames-to-open/|title=MEGADETH + LAMB OF GOD Announce 2020 North American Tour With TRIVIUM And IN FLAMES|publisher=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|access-date=February 10, 2020|date=February 10, 2020|archive-date=February 13, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200213191755/https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/megadeth-lamb-of-god-announce-2020-north-american-tour-trivium-and-in-flames-to-open/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/hatebreed-replaces-in-flames-on-the-metal-tour-of-the-year/|title=HATEBREED Replaces IN FLAMES On 'The Metal Tour Of The Year'|publisher=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|access-date=July 16, 2021|date=July 13, 2021|archive-date=July 15, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210715203414/https://blabbermouth.net/news/hatebreed-replaces-in-flames-on-the-metal-tour-of-the-year/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In February 2020, the band started posting cryptic images and videos possibly pertaining to their new upcoming album on their social media pages. On February 25, the band posted a teaser video on their social media pages teasing a new song titled "Catastrophist", which was released on February 27. At the same time, the band announced their upcoming ninth studio album titled ''[[What the Dead Men Say (album)|What the Dead Men Say]]'' set for release on April 24, 2020.<ref name="loudwire">{{cite web|url=https://loudwire.com/trivium-catastrophist-song-new-album-what-the-dead-men-say/|title=Trivium Debut New Song 'Catastrophist' + Announce New Album 'What The Dead Men Say'|publisher=[[Loudwire]]|access-date=February 27, 2020|date=February 27, 2020|archive-date=February 27, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200227160856/https://loudwire.com/trivium-catastrophist-song-new-album-what-the-dead-men-say/|url-status=live}}</ref>

On March 9, the band previewed "IX" and "Scattering the Ashes" in a new "[[Spawn (comics)|Spawn]]" trailer for ''[[Mortal Kombat 11]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/matthewkheafy/status/1236808370239258625|title=What a freaking honor to have our band @TriviumOfficial in this trailer! title track "What the Dead Men Say" and its corresponding music video.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kerrang.com/the-news/trivium-release-new-song-what-the-dead-men-say/|title=Trivium Release New album release, the band released their third single "Amongst the Shadows & the Stones".<ref>{{Cite In June 2020, Beaulieu revealed the band was already working on the follow-up to ''What the Dead Men Say'' while being in COVID-19 pandemic quarantine, saying the material they've been working on sounded "really pissed-off".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/trivium-is-already-working-on-music-for-follow-up-to-what-the-dead-men-say/|title=TRIVIUM Is Already Working On Music For Follow-Up To 'What The Dead Men Say'|date=June 7, 2020|website=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|access-date=June 9, 2020|archive-date=June 9, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200609051358/https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/trivium-is-already-working-on-music-for-follow-up-to-what-the-dead-men-say/|url-status=live}}</ref>

On September 25, the band's former guitarist and bassist Brent Young died at the age of 37. At the time of his death, he was in the band BlackNova founded with another former Trivium member, drummer Travis Smith.<ref name="BrentSmith">{{cite web|url=https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/former-trivium-bassist-brent-young-dies/|title=Former TRIVIUM Bassist BRENT YOUNG Dies|website=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=September 26, 2020|access-date=September 26, 2020|archive-date=September 27, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200927191406/https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/former-trivium-bassist-brent-young-dies/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="BrentSmith1">{{cite web|author=Greg Kennelty|url=https://metalinjection.net/this-is-just-a-tribute/ex-trivium-bassist-brent-young-has-passed-away|title=Ex-TRIVIUM Bassist Brent Young Has Passed Away|website=Metal Injection|date=September 26, 2020|access-date=September 26, 2020|archive-date=September 27, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200927191546/https://metalinjection.net/this-is-just-a-tribute/ex-trivium-bassist-brent-young-has-passed-away|url-status=live}}</ref>

It is part of a split single to commemorate both bands touring together in Europe and the UK, released on January 27, 2023, on which Heaven Shall Burn covered "Pillars of Serpents" from Trivium's 2003 debut album, ''[[Ember to Inferno]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theprp.com/2022/11/30/news/trivium-heaven-shall-burn-cover-each-other-for-upcoming-new-split/|title=Trivium & Heaven Shall Burn Cover Each Other For Upcoming New Split|publisher=ThePRP|access-date=November 30, 2022|date=January 13, 2023|archive-date=November 30, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221130213236/https://www.theprp.com/2022/11/30/news/trivium-heaven-shall-burn-cover-each-other-for-upcoming-new-split/|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== 20th anniversary tour of ''Ascendancy'', ''Struck Dead'' EP, and upcoming eleventh studio album (2024–present) ===
In celebration of the 20th anniversary of ''Ascendancy'', the band announced 'The Poisoned Ascendancy' Tour with [[Bullet for My Valentine]] co-headlining for 2025, in which Bullet for My Valentine would also be celebrating the 20th anniversary of ''[[The Poison]].''<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 17, 2024 |title=BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE And TRIVIUM Announce North American Dates For 'The Poisoned Ascendancy' Tour |url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/bullet-for-my-valentine-and-trivium-announce-north-american-dates-for-the-poisoned-ascendancy-tour |website=Blabbermouth}}</ref> Trivium also announced that they would be writing their eleventh studio album, which would feature a guest appearance by Bullet for My Valentine vocalist [[Matt Tuck]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 26, 2024 |title=Next TRIVIUM Album Will Feature Appearance From BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE's MATT TUCK |url=https://loadedradio.com/trivium-album-bullet-for-my-valentine-matt-tuck/ |website=Loaded Radio}}</ref> Heafy has stated that the upcoming album will show the band "getting back in the headspace of ''Ascendancy''."<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 26, 2024 |title=Trivium's next album to be influenced by "Ascendancy" |url=https://chaoszine.net/triviums-next-album-to-be-influenced-by-ascendancy/ |website=Chaoszine}}</ref> The band planned to work on the album, set to be released in 2026, after finishing the tour.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 12, 2025 |title=New TRIVIUM Album To Arrive In 2026: 'We've Been Working On Some Stuff', Says COREY BEAULIEU |url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/new-trivium-album-to-arrive-in-2026-weve-been-working-on-some-stuff-says-corey-beaulieu |website=Blabbermouth}}</ref> However, Bullet for My Valentine pulled out of the tour in May 2025, finishing the North American leg, despite initial plans to tour regions such as South America and Australia into the end of 2025, with Gregoletto putting the blame on Tuck.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 12, 2025 |title=Trivium Blame BFMV for Ending Co-Headlining Tour Early |url=https://loudwire.com/trivium-blame-bullet-for-my-valentine-ending-tour-early/ |website=Loudwire}}</ref> Heafy released a statement telling fans "there was an initial plan, and the plan’s changed [...] they’ve got other plans to go do a record, so I respect that", urging fans to "pull back on the negative stuff".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Garner |first=Emily |date=2025-05-14 |title=BFMV and Trivium issue statements on early end to Poisoned Ascendancy… |url=https://www.kerrang.com/bullet-for-my-valentine-trivium-poisoned-ascendancy-tour-drama-matt-tuck-matt-heafy-metal |access-date=2025-05-20 |website=Kerrang! |language=en}}</ref>

On August 7, 2025, the band officially released the single "Bury Me With My Screams", along with its music video, to be part of a new EP, ''Struck Dead'', scheduled for release on October 31, 2025.<ref>{{cite web|author=Surej Singh|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/trivium-announce-new-ep-share-brutal-new-single-bury-me-with-my-screams-3883300|title=Trivium announce new EP, share brutal new single ‘Bury Me With My Screams’|publisher=[[NME]]|access-date=August 7, 2025|date=August 7, 2025}}</ref>

Trivium bio"/> [[progressive metal]],<ref name="Phoenix Times">{{cite web|url=http://www.phoenixnewtimes.com/music/triviums-paolo-gregoletto-prefers-sia-to-taylor-swift-8673597|title=Trivium's Paolo Gregoletto Prefers Sia to Taylor Swift|first=Lauren|last=Wise|date=September 23, 2016|website=[[Phoenix New Times]]|access-date=October 21, 2017|archive-date=August 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170807152959/http://www.phoenixnewtimes.com/music/triviums-paolo-gregoletto-prefers-sia-to-taylor-swift-8673597|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Team Rock - Trivium bio"/><ref name=Allmusic>{{cite web|last=Loftus|first=Johnny|url=https://www.allmusic.com/artist/p603606|title=Trivium - Overview|website=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=April 10, 2010|archive-date=March 3, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110303142421/http://www.allmusic.com/artist/p603606|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Loudwire - Big Four"/> [[melodic death metal]],<ref name="Phoenix Times"/><ref name="Loudwire - Big Four"/> [[groove metal]],<ref name="Team Rock - Trivium bio">{{cite web|url=http://teamrock.com/artist-directory/t/trivium|title=Trivium - Artist Directory|website=TeamRock.com|access-date=October 21, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171112034354/http://teamrock.com/artist-directory/t/trivium|archive-date=November 12, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/deathless-mw0001776861|title=Review of ''Deathless''|first=Phil|last=Freeman|access-date=29 April 2020|publisher=[[AllMusic]]|archive-date=June 11, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200611003557/https://www.allmusic.com/album/deathless-mw0001776861|url-status=live}}</ref> [[alternative metal]],<ref name="Team Rock - Trivium bio"/> and [[power metal]].<ref name="Loudwire - Big Four"/>

Trivium's music mixes "soaring" and "crushing" [[riffs]], dual guitar harmonies, [[double bass drum]] patterns and occasional [[blast beat]]s and breakdowns typical of the metalcore genre. Vocally, Trivium combines both [[singing]] along with heavy [[screaming (music)|screaming]] and [[death growl|growls]]. Trivium has been considered one of the notable [[New wave of American heavy metal]] acts,<ref name="Blabbermouth">{{cite news |title='New Wave Of American Heavy Metal' Book Documents Over 600 Bands |url=http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=44955 |work=[[Blabbermouth.net]] |access-date=April 27, 2008 |archive-date=May 21, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080521104002/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=44955 |url-status=live }}</ref> having been referred to as one of "big four" bands of the movement, along with [[Lamb of God (band)|Lamb of God]], [[Avenged Sevenfold]] and [[Slipknot (band)|Slipknot]].<ref name="Loudwire - Big Four">{{Cite web|last=Blum|first=Jordan|title=The 'Big 4' Bands of 17 Metal Subgenres|url=https://loudwire.com/big-4-bands-metal-subgenres/|access-date=2021-12-17|website=Loudwire|date=November 19, 2021 |language=en|archive-date=September 6, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220906022346/https://loudwire.com/big-4-bands-metal-subgenres/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Their style has evolved over the years: from their earliest work on ''[[Ember to Inferno]]'' through ''[[In Waves (Trivium album)|In Waves]]'', there is a clear thrash influence from [[Metallica]] and [[Machine Head (band)|Machine Head]], as well as a melodic death metal influence from early [[In Flames]].<ref name="MetalHammer">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.metalhammer.co.uk/news/albums-of-the-decade-trivium-ascendancy/|title=Ascendancy Named as album of the decade|date=July 15, 2009|magazine=[[Metal Hammer]]|access-date=July 15, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130412235749/http://www.metalhammer.co.uk/news/albums-of-the-decade-trivium-ascendancy/|archive-date=April 12, 2013|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

Upon the release of their second album ''[[Ascendancy (album)|Ascendancy]]'',<ref name="Ascendancy Received Gold Status">{{cite web|url=http://www.roadrunnerrecords.co.uk/release/The+Crusade|title=Ascendancy Received Gold Status|date=July 15, 2005|website=RoadrunnerRecords.co.uk|access-date=July 15, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090701034150/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.co.uk/release/The+Crusade|archive-date=July 1, 2009|df=mdy-all}}</ref> Trivium were identified as [[melodic metalcore]] with strong elements of thrash metal, with the third track on the album "[[Pull Harder on the Strings of Your Martyr]]" becoming a permanent fixture in the band's set lists and the rest of the album selling itself to gold status.<ref name="Ascendancy Received Gold Status" /> ''Ascendancy'' was even featured as one of [[Metal Hammer|Metal Hammer's]] Albums of the Decade.<ref name="MetalHammer" /> ''[[The Crusade (album)|The Crusade]]'' was seen as a major shift in musical direction due to the change in vocal style, namely the absence of screaming, and some of the melodies featured.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.roadrunnerrecords.co.uk/release/The+Crusade|title=Crusade Changes Direction|date=July 15, 2005|website=RoadrunnerRecords.co.uk|access-date=July 15, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090701034150/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.co.uk/release/The+Crusade|archive-date=July 1, 2009|df=mdy-all}}</ref> ''The Crusade'' was a much more thrash-oriented album and contained different lyrical themes such as current affairs and famous killings.

''Shogun'' has a heavy Japanese influence on its title track as well as the first single release "Kirisute Gomen", which translates to "[[Kiri sute gomen|authorization to cut and leave]]". Acknowledging Matt Heafy's Japanese heritage,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thrashhits.com/2008/08/album-trivium-shogun/|title=Thrashhits Review on Shogun|date=July 15, 2009|publisher=Thrash Hits|access-date=July 15, 2009|archive-date=April 15, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090415164339/http://www.thrashhits.com/2008/08/album-trivium-shogun/|url-status=live}}</ref> the album also was described more favorably as more their own style, as previous references to Trivium sounding like Metallica had been made on the back of ''The Crusade''.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.stylusmagazine.com/reviews/trivium/the-crusade.htm|title=The Crusade Review (Hetfield Reference)|date=July 15, 2009|magazine=Stylus Magazine|access-date=July 15, 2009}}</ref> ''The Crusade'' made sparing use of [[seven-string guitar]]s, which were featured heavily on ''Shogun''.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Trivium - The Crusade (album review 9) {{!}} Sputnikmusic|url = https://www.sputnikmusic.com/review/9696/Trivium-The-Crusade/|website = www.sputnikmusic.com|access-date = 2015-09-26|archive-date = September 2, 2023|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20230902224417/https://www.sputnikmusic.com/review/9696/Trivium-The-Crusade/|url-status = live}}</ref>

On ''In Waves'', the band featured a sound closer to ''Ascendancy'' than ''The Crusade'' and ''Shogun''. Instead of being in drop D like on ''Ascendancy'', the band went half a step lower to drop C#. The album has several songs, such as 'Built to Fall' or 'Dusk Dismantled', featuring mostly clean vocals or solely screamed vocals from Heafy. Seven-string guitars once again returned on ''[[Silence in the Snow]]'' tuned to B-flat,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.trivium.org/spotifystories|title=The Story And Sound Behind Silence In The Snow|website=Trivium.org|access-date=21 October 2017|archive-date=December 8, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208130154/http://www.trivium.org/spotifystories|url-status=live}}</ref> and have since been used in subsequent albums along with the previously used six-string drop C# tuning, and occasionally seven-string drop G# tuning.

===Influences===
Trivium has stated that they are influenced by musical groups such as [[Opeth]], [[Nevermore]], [[Dream Theater]], [[Emperor (Norwegian band)|Emperor]], [[Slipknot (band)|Slipknot]], [[In Flames]], [[At the Gates]], [[Arch Enemy]], [[Machine Head (band)|Machine Head]], [[Guns N' Roses]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://spinitloud.com/?p=112 |title=Trivium |website=Spinitloud.com |access-date=2014-03-04 |archive-date=October 15, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131015032854/http://spinitloud.com/?p=112 |url-status=usurped }}</ref> [[Metallica]], [[Iron Maiden]], [[Megadeth]], [[Ozzy Osbourne]], [[Mercyful Fate]], [[Hellhammer]], [[Celtic Frost]], [[Slayer]], [[Pantera]], [[Dio (band)|Dio]], [[Black Sabbath]], [[Judas Priest]], [[Annihilator (band)|Annihilator]], [[Testament (band)|Testament]], [[Cannibal Corpse]], [[Obituary (band)|Obituary]], [[Killswitch Engage]], [[Skid Row (American band)|Skid Row]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.metalunderground.com/reviews/details.cfm?releaseid=520 |title=Trivium - "The Crusade" CD Review - in Metal Reviews |publisher=Metal Underground.com |access-date=2014-03-04 |archive-date=October 15, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131015030337/http://www.metalunderground.com/reviews/details.cfm?releaseid=520 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Angra (band)|Angra]], [[Martyr (band)|Martyr]] and [[Death (metal band)|Death]].<ref name="autogenerated1">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.metalhammer.co.uk/news/triviums-matt-heafy-my-top-ten-essential-metal-albums/ |title=Blog Archive » Trivium's Matt Heafy: My Top Ten Essential Metal Albums |magazine=[[Metal Hammer]] |access-date=July 9, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.metalinside.de/interview/trivium|title=Trivium - metalinside|website=Metalinside.de|access-date=October 21, 2017|archive-date=May 20, 2017|archive-url=https://archive.today/20170520143454/http://www.metalinside.de/interview/trivium|url-status=live}}</ref> In an 2022 interview with ''[[Premier Guitar]]'', Heafy stated that the band's early sound was a conscious combination of the sounds of the "metal greats" Megadeth, Metallica, Pantera, Testament and Slayer; Gothenburg melodic death metal, namely In Flames' second through sixth albums; black metal; death metal; and German metalcore, particularly [[Caliban (band)|Caliban]] and [[Heaven Shall Burn]].<ref>{{cite AV media |people=[[Matt Heafy]] |date=May 3, 2022 |title= Trivium's Matt Heafy on In Flames' "Artifacts of the Black Rain" |url=https://www.premierguitar.com/videos/hooked/trivium |access-date=May 6, 2022 |time=3m30s |publisher=[[Premier Guitar]]}}</ref> In a 2024 interview with ''[[NME]]'', Heafy additionally claimed that ''Ascendancy'''s influenced were "the classic metal bands that everyone loved alongside melodic death metal, metalcore and [[emo]]."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Shutler |first1=Ali Shutler |title=Trivium and Bullet For My Valentine talk 'Poisoned Ascendancy' tour and new music: "20 years is a long time to be making an impact" |url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/trivium-and-bullet-for-my-valentine-talk-poisoned-ascendancy-tour-and-new-music-ticket-details-tour-dates-onsale-3591867 |website=[[NME]] |date=February 23, 2024 |access-date=25 June 2025}}</ref> He separately asserted that "without Iron Maiden, Trivium surely wouldn't exist."<ref>{{cite magazine |date=2008-07-16 |title=The making of Maiden Heaven |url=http://www.kerrang.com/blog/2008/07/the_making_of_maiden_heaven.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130501010936/http://www.kerrang.com/blog/2008/07/the_making_of_maiden_heaven.html |archive-date=May 1, 2013 |access-date=2015-09-26 |magazine=[[Kerrang!]]}}</ref>

In an interview with [[Roadrunner Records]], Heafy stated he listened to different types of music during different stages of his life. As a child, he listened to [[pop punk]] and [[ska punk]] bands like [[Blink-182]], and [[Reel Big Fish]]. Heafy also lists bands like Pantera, Slayer, [[Cryptopsy]], [[Children of Bodom]], [[Dark Tranquillity]], [[Mercenary (band)|Mercenary]], [[Manowar (band)|Manowar]], [[Armored Saint]], [[Darkthrone]], [[3 Inches of Blood]], [[Krisiun]], [[Fear Factory]], [[Dimmu Borgir]], [[Dark Funeral]], [[Anorexia Nervosa (band)|Anorexia Nervosa]], [[Poison the Well (band)|Poison the Well]], [[Hatebreed]], [[Yngwie Malmsteen]], [[Led Zeppelin]], [[AC/DC (band)|AC/DC]], [[Aerosmith]], [[Queen (band)|Queen]], [[Van Halen]], [[Dashboard Confessional]], [[Further Seems Forever]], [[Depeche Mode]], [[The Beatles]], and more.<ref>{{cite web |last=Records |first=Roadrunner |url=http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/news/gear-nerd-trivium-s-matt-heafy-part-1 |title=Gear Nerd:Trivium's Matt Heafy Part 1 |publisher=Roadrunner Records |date=2011-07-12 |access-date=2014-03-04 |archive-date=July 26, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120726003233/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/news/gear-nerd-trivium-s-matt-heafy-part-1 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Metal, the military, food and nerddom: A one-on-one chat with Trivium's Matt Heafy | date=April 14, 2020 | url=https://www.militarytimes.com/off-duty/military-culture/2018/09/20/metal-the-military-food-and-nerd-dom-a-one-on-one-chat-with-triviums-matt-heafy/ }}</ref>

===Lyrical themes===
{{More citations needed|date=March 2025}}

Heafy been the primary lyricist since his early days as a member. He is known for his poetic style of lyrics and the usage of archaic words. Growing up, Heafy experienced [[anxiety]], teenage [[angst]], and occasional thoughts of [[suicide]]; several songs from the album ''Ascendancy'', such as "Rain", "Suffocating Sight", and "Departure", deal with these issues. Although not a victim himself, he also wrote the song "A Gunshot to the Head of Trepidation" on the topic of [[domestic violence]] and [[child abuse]], inspired by the stories of some of his peers.

Lyrical themes on the album ''The Crusade'' includes famous killings. "Entrance of the Conflagration" is about [[Andrea Yates]]'s murder of her five children, "Unrepentant" is about Nazir Ahmad's murder of his three daughters and stepdaughter, "Contempt Breeds Contamination" is about the death of [[Amadou Diallo]], and "And Sadness Will Sear" is based upon the murder of [[Matthew Shepard]].

Many of the songs on ''Shogun'' draw lyrical inspiration from [[Greek mythology]]. "Into the Mouth of Hell We March" and "Torn Between Scylla and Charybdis" detail the story of [[Odysseus]] choosing whether to face the giant whirlpool [[Charybdis]] or the six-headed monster [[Scylla]]. "He Who Spawned the Furies" is about the [[Titan (mythology)|Titan]] [[Cronus|Cronos]] devouring his children and castrating his father [[Uranus (mythology)|Uranus]], creating [[Aphrodite]] and the [[Erinyes|Erinýes]] (the Furies). "Of Prometheus and the Crucifix" references the daily torment of [[Prometheus]] and alludes to [[crucifixion of Jesus]]. "Like Callisto to a Star in Heaven" is written from the perspective of the [[nymph]] [[Callisto (mythology)|Callisto]], detailing her rape and impregnation by [[Zeus]] and her transformations into a bear and into [[Ursa Major]]. Mythological lyrics returned on ''[[In the Court of the Dragon]]''. Inspired by fantasy literature, the band made up its own mythology on the album.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://knotfest.com/culture/matt-heafy-talks-overcoming-negativity-and-the-new-trivium-album-in-the-court-of-the-dragon/|title=Matt Heafy Talks Overcoming Negativity and the New Trivium Album 'In the Court of the Dragon'|work=[[Knotfest]]|last=Delgadillo|first=Nicolás|date=September 9, 2021|accessdate=October 10, 2021|archive-date=October 10, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211010132552/https://knotfest.com/culture/matt-heafy-talks-overcoming-negativity-and-the-new-trivium-album-in-the-court-of-the-dragon/|url-status=live}}</ref> Lyrical content on ''[[The Sin and the Sentence]]'' and ''[[What the Dead Men Say (album)|What the Dead Men Say]]'' were inspired by modern aspects of life, such as [[social media]] and [[artificial intelligence]] as well as general themes such as [[war]], [[history]] and [[religion]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://teamrock.com/feature/2017-10-19/triviums-track-by-track-guide-to-the-sin-and-the-sentence|title=Trivium's track-by-track guide to The Sin And The Sentence|date=October 19, 2017|website=Teamrock.com|access-date=November 23, 2017|archive-date=November 8, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108160218/http://teamrock.com/feature/2017-10-19/triviums-track-by-track-guide-to-the-sin-and-the-sentence|url-status=live}}</ref>

'''The Cult''' are <!-- This article is written in British-English, which treats collective nouns as plurals. Please do not change "are" to "is". See WP:ENGVAR for more info. --> an English [[Rock music|rock]] band formed in [[Bradford]] in 1983. Before settling on their current name in January 1984, the band had performed under the name '''Death Cult''', which was an evolution of the name of lead vocalist [[Ian Astbury]]'s previous band [[Southern Death Cult]]. They gained a dedicated following in the United Kingdom in the mid-1980s as a [[post-punk]] and [[gothic rock]] band, with singles such as "[[She Sells Sanctuary]]", before breaking into the mainstream in the United States in the late 1980s establishing themselves as a [[hard rock]] band with singles such as "[[Love Removal Machine]]". Since its initial formation in 1983, the band have had various line-ups: the longest-serving members are Astbury and guitarist [[Billy Duffy]], who are also their two main songwriters.

The Cult's debut studio album ''[[Dreamtime (The Cult album)|Dreamtime]]'' was released in 1984 to moderate success, with its lead single "[[Spiritwalker (song)|Spiritwalker]]" reaching No.&nbsp;1 on the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]]. Their second studio album, ''[[Love (The Cult album)|Love]]'' (1985), was also successful, charting at No.&nbsp;4 in the UK and including singles such as "She Sells Sanctuary" and "[[Rain (The Cult song)|Rain]]". The band's third studio album, ''[[Electric (The Cult album)|Electric]]'' (1987), launched them to new heights of success, also peaking at No.&nbsp;4 in the UK and charting highly in other territories, and spawned the hit singles "Love Removal Machine", "Lil' Devil" and "Wild Flower". On that album, the Cult supplemented their post-punk sound with hard rock; the polish on this new sound was facilitated by producer [[Rick Rubin]]. After moving to [[Los Angeles]], where the band have been based for the remainder of their career,<ref>{{cite news|title=Everynight Charley's Manhattan Beat: Michael Monroe, Cannibal Corpse, The Cult and More|url=http://www.theaquarian.com/2016/03/16/everynight-charleys-manhattan-beat-michael-monroe-cannibal-corpse-the-cult-and-more/|newspaper=[[The Aquarian Weekly]]|date=16 March 2016|access-date=6 June 2017|archive-date=11 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170711011839/http://www.theaquarian.com/2016/03/16/everynight-charleys-manhattan-beat-michael-monroe-cannibal-corpse-the-cult-and-more/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Ian Astbury net worth!|url=http://anetworth.net/ian-astbury-net-worth/|publisher=anetworth.net|access-date=6 June 2017|archive-date=10 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171110005002/http://anetworth.net/ian-astbury-net-worth/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=The Cult at Mountain Winery – Tickets – The Mountain Winery – Saratoga, CA – June 5th, 2016|url=http://www.ticketfly.com/event/1158397-cult-mountain-winery-saratoga/|publisher=ticketfly.com|access-date=6 June 2017|archive-date=10 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171110114629/https://www.ticketfly.com/event/1158397-cult-mountain-winery-saratoga/|url-status=live}}</ref> the Cult continued the musical experimentation of ''Electric'' with its follow-up studio album ''[[Sonic Temple]]'' (1989), which marked their first collaboration with [[Bob Rock]], who would produce several of the band's subsequent studio albums. ''Sonic Temple'' was their most successful studio album to that point, entering the Top 10 on the UK and US charts, and included one of the band's most popular songs "[[Fire Woman]]".

By the time of their fifth studio album ''[[Ceremony (The Cult album)|Ceremony]]'' (1991), tensions and creative differences began to surface between the band members. This resulted in the recording sessions for ''Ceremony'' being held without a stable line-up, leaving Astbury and Duffy as the only two official members, and featuring support from session musicians on bass guitar and drums. The ongoing tension had carried over within the next few years, during which the band one more studio album – ''[[The Cult (album)|The Cult]]'' (1994) – before disbanding in 1995.<ref name="BIOAMG" /> The Cult reformed in 1999 and released their seventh studio album ''[[Beyond Good and Evil (album)|Beyond Good and Evil]]'' two years later. The commercial failure of the album and resurfaced tensions led to the band's second dissolution in 2002. The Cult reunited once again in 2006, and have since released four more studio albums: ''[[Born into This]]'' (2007), ''[[Choice of Weapon]]'' (2012), ''[[Hidden City (album)|Hidden City]]'' (2016) and ''[[Under the Midnight Sun]]'' (2022).

==History==
===Early history (1981–1984)===
{{Main|Southern Death Cult}}
The band's origins can be traced to 1981, in [[Bradford]], [[Yorkshire]], where lead vocalist and songwriter Ian Astbury formed a band called [[Southern Death Cult]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.deathrock.com/southerndeathcult/main.html| title = The Southern Death Cult | work = Deathrock.com | access-date = 15 January 2007 }}</ref> The name was chosen with a [[Double entendre|double meaning]]. It was derived from the academic term ''Southern Death Cult'', used to describe a cluster of 14th-century Native American groups now classified as the [[Southeastern Ceremonial Complex]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.mississippian-artifacts.com/html/shellorn.html | title = Shell Ornaments | work = Mississippian-Artifacts.com | access-date = 15 January 2007 | archive-date = 8 February 2007 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070208121801/http://www.mississippian-artifacts.com/html/shellorn.html | url-status = live }}</ref> The name Southern Death Cult also inspired by what the band viewed was the centralisation of political and economic power in Southern England (including the power of the music industry); there has long been a perceived notion of an England [[North–South divide in the United Kingdom|North–South divide]] based on social, historic and economic reasons.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://thearchive.free.fr/arch-sdeathcult.htm| title = Southern Death Cult NME 1982| work = [[NME]]| access-date = 15 January 2007| archive-date = 7 February 2012| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120207071143/http://thearchive.free.fr/arch-sdeathcult.htm| url-status = live}}</ref> Astbury was joined by guitarist Buzz Burrows, bassist Barry Jepson and drummer [[Aki Nawaz|Aki Nawaz Qureshi]]; they performed their first show at the Queen's Hall in their hometown of Bradford on 29 October 1981.<ref name="redsun">{{cite web| url = http://www.redsunrecords.com/product_info.php?products_id=751&cPath=78&language=fr| title = Southern Death Cult| work = Red Sun Press| access-date = 15 January 2007| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120210140717/http://www.redsunrecords.com/product_info.php?products_id=751&cPath=78&language=fr| archive-date = 10 February 2012| url-status = dead}}</ref> The band were at the forefront of an emerging style of music, in the form of [[post-punk]] and [[gothic rock]], they achieved critical acclaim from the press and music fans.<ref name="redsun" />

The band signed to independent record label [[Situation Two]], an offshoot of [[Beggars Banquet Records]], and released a three-track, triple A-side single, "Moya", in 1982. They toured through England headlining some shows and touring with [[Bauhaus (band)|Bauhaus]] and [[Theatre of Hate]].<ref name="redsun" /> Southern Death Cult played their final performance in [[Manchester]] during February 1983, meaning after only 16 months the band were over. A compilation album named ''[[The Southern Death Cult (album)|The Southern Death Cult]]'' was released, this being a collection of the single, radio sessions with [[John Peel]] for [[BBC Radio 1|Radio One]] and live performances – one of which an audience member recorded with a tape recorder.<ref name="redsun" />

In April 1983, Astbury teamed up with guitarist [[Billy Duffy]] and formed the band "Death Cult". Duffy had been in [[the Nosebleeds]] (along with [[Morrissey]], later of [[the Smiths]]), Lonesome No More and then [[Theatre of Hate]]. In addition to Astbury and Duffy, the band also included bassist [[Jamie Stewart (English musician)|Jamie Stewart]] and drummer Raymond Taylor Smith (later known as [[Ray Mondo]]), both from the [[Harrow, London]] based post-punk band, [[Ritual (post-punk band)|Ritual]]. Death Cult made their live debut in [[Oslo]], Norway on 25 July 1983 and also released the ''[[Death Cult (EP)|Death Cult]]'' [[Extended play|EP]] in the same month, then toured through mainland Europe. In September 1983, a deal was made to switch drummers, Mondo would be replaced by [[Nigel Preston]], as the drummer for [[Sex Gang Children]] and Preston would join Death Cult. The single "[[Gods Zoo]]" was released in October 1983. Another European tour, with UK dates, followed that autumn. To tone down their name's gothic connotations and gain broader appeal, the band changed its name to "the Cult" in January 1984 before appearing on the [[Channel 4]] television show, ''[[The Tube (1982 TV series)|The Tube]]''.

The Cult's debut studio album, ''[[Dreamtime (The Cult album)|Dreamtime]]'', was recorded at [[Rockfield Studios]], in [[Monmouth]], Wales in 1984. The record was to be produced by Joe Julian, but after recording the drum tracks, the band decided to replace him with John Brand. Brand produced the record, but guitarist Duffy has said the drum tracks were produced by Julian, as Preston had become unreliable.

The band recorded the songs which later became known as "Butterflies", "(The) Gimmick", "A Flower in the Desert", "Horse Nation", "[[Spiritwalker (song)|Spiritwalker]]", "Bad Medicine (Waltz)", "Dreamtime", "With Love" (later known as "Ship of Fools", and also "Sea and Sky"), "Bone Bag", "Too Young", "83rd Dream", and one untitled outtake. It is unknown what the outtake was, or whether it was developed into a song at a later date. Songs like "Horse Nation" showed Astbury's intense interest in Native American issues, with the lyrics to "Horse Nation", "See them prancing, they come neighing, to a horse nation", taken almost verbatim from the book ''[[Bury My Heart at Wounded Knee]]'' (1970), while "[[Spiritwalker (song)|Spiritwalker]]" dealt with [[shamanism]], and the record's title and title track are overtly influenced by Australian [[Indigenous Australians|Aboriginal]] beliefs.

On 4 April 1984, the Cult released the single "Spiritwalker", which reached No.&nbsp;1 on the independent charts in the UK, and acted as a teaser for their forthcoming studio album ''[[Dreamtime (The Cult album)|Dreamtime]]''. This was followed that summer by a second single, "[[Go West (Crazy Spinning Circles)]]", before the release of ''Dreamtime'' in September; the album reached No.&nbsp;21 in the UK, and sold over 100,000 copies in the UK alone. On 12 July 1984, the band recorded five songs at the [[BBC]] Maida Vale 5 studio for a [[Richard Skinner (broadcaster)|Richard Skinner]] session. Before and after the album's release, the Cult toured throughout Europe and England before recording another single, "[[Ressurection Joe]]" (UK No.&nbsp;74), released that December. Following a Christmas support slot with [[Big Country]], the Cult toured Europe with support from [[The Mission (band)|the Mission]] (then-called [[The Sisterhood (gothic rock band)|the Sisterhood]]). ''Dreamtime'' was released initially only in the UK, but after its success, and as the Cult's popularity grew worldwide, it was issued in approximately 30 countries.

===Mainstream success (1985–1990)===
In May 1985, the Cult released their fourth single, "[[She Sells Sanctuary]]", which peaked at No.&nbsp;15 in the UK and spent 23 weeks in the Top 100. The song was recently voted No.&nbsp;18 in [[VH1]]'s Indie 100{{when|date=March 2017}}. In the following month, after his increasingly erratic behaviour, Preston was fired from the band. Big Country's drummer [[Mark Brzezicki]] was picked to replace Preston, and was also included in the music video for "She Sells Sanctuary". The Cult then finished recording their second studio album, ''[[Love (The Cult album)|Love]]'', in July and August 1985. The band's music and image shifted from their punk-oriented roots to 1960s [[Psychedelia#In popular culture|psychedelia]] influences. ''Love'' was a chart success, peaking at No.&nbsp;4 in the UK and selling 100,000 copies there<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bpi.co.uk/certifiedawards/search.aspx |title=British Phonographic Industry certifications database |publisher=Bpi.co.uk |access-date=16 July 2011 |archive-date=2 July 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160702214649/http://www.bpi.co.uk/certifiedawards/search.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref> toward a total of 500,000 copies throughout Europe, as well as 100,000 in Australia and 500,000 copies in the United States.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.riaa.com/goldandplatinumdata.php?table=SEARCH |title=Recording Industry Association of America certifications database |publisher=Riaa.com |access-date=16 July 2011 |archive-date=26 June 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070626050454/http://www.riaa.com/goldandplatinumdata.php?table=SEARCH |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Love'' reached number 20 on the charts in the Netherlands, where it remained for 32 weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://charts.nz/showitem.asp?interpret=The+Cult&titel=Love&cat=a|title=The Cult - Love|website=Charts.nz|access-date=3 January 2021|archive-date=22 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200922142527/https://charts.nz/showitem.asp?interpret=The+Cult&titel=Love&cat=a|url-status=live}}</ref> To date,{{when|date=January 2020}} the record has sold over two and a half million copies worldwide.

From late September 1985 to June 1986, the band went on a worldwide tour with new drummer [[Les Warner]] (who had played with [[Julian Lennon]] and [[Johnny Thunders]]). Two more singles from the ''Love'' album followed; "Rain" (charting in the UK at No.&nbsp;17) and "[[Revolution (The Cult song)|Revolution]]" (charting in the UK at No.&nbsp;30). Neither charted in the US. Another single, "Nirvana", was issued only in Poland. The album version of "Rain", as well as the remix "(Here Comes the) Rain", were used in the Italian horror film ''[[Demons 2]]'' (1986). Once back in England, the band booked themselves into the [[The Manor Studio|Manor Studios]] in Oxfordshire, with producer Steve Brown (who had produced ''Love''), and recorded over a dozen new songs. The band were unhappy with the sound of their new studio album, titled ''Peace'', and they decided to go to New York so producer [[Rick Rubin]] could remix the first single, "[[Love Removal Machine]]".

Rubin agreed to work with the band, but only if they re-recorded the song. Rubin eventually talked them into re-recording the entire album. The band's record company, Beggars Banquet, was displeased with this, as two months and £250,000 had already been spent on the record. However, after hearing the initial New York recording, Beggars Banquet agreed to proceed. The first single, "Love Removal Machine", was released in February 1987, and the new version of the album appeared in April that year, now renamed as ''[[Electric (The Cult album)|Electric]]'', reaching No.&nbsp;4 and eventually outselling ''Love''. The band toured with [[Kid Chaos]] (also known as "Haggis" and "The Kid") on bass guitar, with Stewart on rhythm guitar. Two more singles, "Lil Devil" and "Wild Flower", were released during 1987. A few tracks from the original ''Peace'' album appeared on the single versions of "Love Removal Machine", and "Lil Devil". The full ''Peace'' album would not be released until 2000, when it was included as Disc 3 of the ''Rare Cult'' box set.

In the US, the Cult, now consisting of Astbury, Duffy, Stewart, Warner and Kid Chaos, were supported by a then-unknown [[Guns N' Roses]]. The band also appeared at [[Roskilde Festival]] in Denmark in June 1987. During the Australian part of the world tour, the band wrecked £30,000 worth of equipment, and as a result they could not tour Japan as no company would rent them new equipment. At the end of the tour the ''Electric'' album had been certified Gold in the UK, and sold roughly 3 million copies worldwide, but the band were barely speaking to each other by then. Haggis left the band at the end of the ''Electric'' tour to form [[The Four Horsemen (band)|the Four Horsemen]] for Rubin's [[American Recordings (US)|Def American]] label. Astbury and Duffy fired Warner and their management team Grant/Edwards, and moved to [[Los Angeles]] with Stewart. Warner sued the band several times for his firing, as well as for what he considered were unpaid royalties for his performance on the ''Electric'' album, resulting in lengthy court battles. The Cult signed a new management deal and wrote 21 new songs for their next album.

For the next studio album, Stewart returned to playing bass guitar, and John Webster was brought in to play keyboards. The band used Chris Taylor to play drums during rehearsals and record the demos, with future [[Kiss (band)|Kiss]] drummer [[Eric Singer]] performing during the second demo recording sessions. The Cult eventually recruited session drummer [[Mickey Curry]] to fill the drumming role and [[Aerosmith]] sound engineer, [[Bob Rock]], to produce. Recorded in [[Vancouver]] from October to December 1988, and released in April of the following year, ''[[Sonic Temple]]'' went Top 10 in both the UK and the US, where it was certified Gold and Platinum respectively. The band went on tour in support of the new album and new single "[[Fire Woman]]" (UK No.&nbsp;15) (NZ No.&nbsp;1), with yet another new drummer, [[Matt Sorum]], and Webster as keyboardist. The next single, "Edie (Ciao Baby)" (UK No.&nbsp;25) has become a regular song at concerts for many years.

In Europe, the band toured with [[Aerosmith]], and in the US, after releasing another single "Sun King" (UK No.&nbsp;42), they spent 1989 touring in support of [[Metallica]] before heading out on their own headlining tour later that same year. The fourth and final single, "Sweet Soul Sister" (UK No.&nbsp;38), was released in February 1990, with the video having been filmed at [[Wembley Arena]], London, on 25 November 1989. "Sweet Soul Sister" was partially written in [[Paris]] and was inspired by the [[bohemianism|bohemian]] lifestyle of that city. Released as a single in February 1990, the song was another hit in the UK, and reportedly reached number one on the rock charts in Brazil. After playing a show in [[Atlanta]] in February 1990, the band's management told Astbury that his father had just died of cancer; as a result, the remainder of the tour was cancelled after a final leg of shows were performed in April. After the tour ended, the band were on the verge of breaking up due to Stewart retiring and moving to Canada to be with his wife, and Sorum leaving to join [[Guns N' Roses]].

In 1990, Astbury organised the [[A Gathering of the Tribes|Gathering of the Tribes]] festival in Los Angeles and [[San Francisco]] with artists such as [[Soundgarden]], [[Ice-T]], [[Indigo Girls]], [[Queen Latifah]], [[Iggy Pop]], [[The Charlatans (English band)|the Charlatans]], [[the Cramps]] and [[Public Enemy]] appearing. This two-day festival drew 40,000 people. Also in 1990, a ten CD box set was released in the UK, containing rare songs from the Cult's singles. The CDs in this box set were all issued as [[picture disc]]s with [[washi paper]] covers, housed in a white box called ''Singles Collection'', or a black box called ''E.P. Collection '84 - '90''. In 1991, director [[Oliver Stone]] offered Astbury the role of [[Jim Morrison]] in Stone's film ''[[The Doors (film)|The Doors]]''. He declined the role because he was not happy with the way Morrison was represented in the film,{{citation needed|date=March 2015}} and the role was ultimately played by [[Val Kilmer]].

===''Ceremony'' and the lawsuit (1991–1993)===
By 1991, Astbury and Duffy were writing again for their next studio album. During the demo recordings, Todd Hoffman and [[James Kottak]] played bass guitar and drums, respectively. During the actual album recording sessions, Curry was recruited again to play drums, with [[Charley Drayton]] on bass guitar, and various other performers. Astbury and Duffy's working relationship had disintegrated by that time, with the two men reportedly rarely even being in the studio together during recording.{{citation needed|date=May 2013}} The resulting studio album ''[[Ceremony (The Cult album)|Ceremony]]'' was released in September 1991 to mixed responses. The album climbed to US No.&nbsp;34, but sales were not as impressive as the previous three studio albums, only selling around one million copies worldwide. Only two official singles were released from the record: "Wild Hearted Son" (UK No.&nbsp;34, Canada No.&nbsp;41) and "Heart of Soul" (UK No.&nbsp;50), although "White" was released as a single only in Canada, "Sweet Salvation" was released as a single (as "Dulce Salvación") in Argentina in 1992, and the title track "Ceremony" was released in Spain.

The Cult's Ceremonial Stomp tour went through Europe in 1991 and North America in 1992. In 1991 the Cult played a show at the [[Marquee Club]] in London, which was recorded and released in February 1993, packaged with some vinyl UK copies of their first greatest hits release. Only a handful of CD copies of it were ever manufactured originally, however it was subsequently reissued on CD in 1999. An incomplete [[Bootleg recording|bootleg]] video of this show is also in circulation.

The band were sued by the parents of the Native American boy pictured on the cover of ''Ceremony'', for alleged exploitation and for the unauthorised use of the child's image. The parents stated that the boy felt he had been cursed by the band's burning of his image, and was "emotionally scarred."<ref name="titleWRONG RITE? | Ceremony | Pop Culture News | News | Entertainment Weekly">{{cite magazine |url=http://www.ew.com/article/1992/06/19/cult-faces-legal-battle-sioux |title=Wrong Rite? |magazine=Entertainment Weekly |access-date=31 March 2008 |first=Sharon |last=Isaak |date=19 June 1992 |archive-date=9 October 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081009195457/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,310840,00.html |url-status=live }}</ref> This image of the boy is also burned in the video for "Wild Hearted Son". This lawsuit delayed the release of ''Ceremony'' in many countries including South Korea and Thailand, which did not see the album's release until late 1992, and it was unreleased in Turkey until the Cult played several shows in [[Istanbul]] in June 1993.
